item.title: Bhoomi Trivedi
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Bhoomi Trivedi

Playback Female Singer

Bhoomi Trivedi is an Indian singer known for her notable contributions to the Hindi film industry. She hails from a musical family in Vadodara, Gujarat. Bhoomi developed a passion for music from a young age and began her musical journey while she was in the 8th grade. Her father, who is an employee of the Railways, has a keen interest in singing, while her mother is a folk singer with her own music group. Bhoomi's elder sister is an engineer and a trained Bharata Natyam dancer.

 

In 2007, Bhoomi Trivedi auditioned for the reality show Indian Idol 3 but had to quit due to jaundice. The following year, she auditioned again for Indian Idol 4 but had to leave the show due to the unfortunate demise of her aunt from breast cancer. However, she made a comeback in Indian Idol 5 and finished as the runner-up. During her audition, she impressed the judges by singing a mix of the Gujarati portion of the rap song "Blood Brothers" by Karmacy and "Wannabe" by Spice Girls.

 

Bhoomi's Bollywood career began with the 2012 film Prem Mayee, where she sang the song "Bahne Dey." However, she gained widespread recognition and fame with her rendition of the song "Ram Chahe Leela" in Sanjay Leela Bhansali's 2013 film Goliyon Ki Raasleela: Ram-Leela, featuring Priyanka Chopra. Initially approached to pen Gujarati lyrics and sing a part of a song, Bhoomi impressed Bhansali with her unique voice, leading to her prominent role in the film's soundtrack. Her rendition in "Ram Chahe Leela" received praise from both the audience and critics.

Apart from her Bollywood songs, Bhoomi Trivedi has also recorded songs for various Gujarati films. Notably, she recorded the song "Vaagyo Re Dhol" for the national award-winning film Hellaro. Her versatile singing skills and powerful vocals have earned her accolades and recognition in the music industry. Bhoomi continues to enthrall listeners with her soulful renditions and remains a prominent figure in the Indian music scene.

Charu Semwal

Playback Female Singer

Charu Semwal, a finalist of Indian Idol Season 3, is known for her memorable performances. She has showcased her talent not only on the reality show but also in various other platforms.

 

Charu has lent her voice to advertisements, including the Mine Diamond TVC featuring the renowned actress Kareena Kapoor Khan. This indicates her versatility as a singer, as she has had the opportunity to contribute to commercial projects alongside popular celebrities.

 

In addition to her work in advertisements, Charu has also impressed audiences with her cover song of "Kaun Mera." Cover songs allow artists to showcase their own interpretation and rendition of popular tracks, highlighting their unique vocal abilities.

Charu's talent and hard work have granted her the opportunity to perform in numerous shows, both private and corporate, across India. She has even had the chance to perform internationally, sharing the stage with renowned singers like Sunidhi Chauhan, Mika Singh, Sukhwinder Singh, and Pritam. Her performances have been attended by some of the biggest celebrities, including Hugh Jackman, Aishwarya Rai, Shah Rukh Khan, and Amitabh Bachchan.

 

With her melodious voice and enthusiastic performances, Charu Semwal has become a favorite among audiences. She has the ability to captivate and engage the crowd, making any party or event lively and enjoyable

Playback Female Singer

Chandreyee Bhattacharya is a talented Indian singer known for her mesmerizing vocals and versatility in various genres of music. Born with an innate passion for singing, Chandreyee began her musical journey at a young age and quickly made a mark in the industry with her soulful voice and exceptional talent.

 

With a distinct style and a captivating stage presence, Chandreyee has become a prominent figure in the music scene. Her ability to effortlessly switch between classical, semi-classical, and contemporary genres sets her apart from her peers. Whether it's a melodious classical composition or a foot-tapping Bollywood number, Chandreyee's vocal range and emotive delivery leave a lasting impact on listeners.

 

Her dedication to her craft is evident in her meticulous approach to each performance, making her a favorite among music enthusiasts. Chandreyee has garnered widespread acclaim and has been recognized with several prestigious awards for her contributions to the industry.

 

With her passion, talent, and captivating presence, Chandreyee Bhattacharya continues to enthrall audiences and establish herself as a prominent singer in the Indian music industry. Her musical journey is one that promises continued success and a growing fan base.

item.content:encoded:
Celina Sharma

Playback Female Singer

Celina Sharma is a rising star in the music industry, captivating audiences with her mesmerizing vocals and heartfelt performances. Born with a passion for music, she began her journey at a young age and has quickly become a force to be reckoned with. Hailing from Australia, Sharma's unique blend of pop, R&B, and soul has garnered widespread acclaim and a dedicated fanbase.

 

Known for her powerful yet soulful voice, Sharma effortlessly weaves emotion into her music, creating a deeply personal connection with listeners. Her songs touch upon themes of love, self-discovery, and empowerment, resonating with audiences across the globe. With a diverse range of musical influences, including artists like Beyoncé and Amy Winehouse, she brings a fresh and modern sound to the industry.

 

In addition to her undeniable talent, Celina Sharma possesses an undeniable charisma and stage presence, captivating audiences with her magnetic performances. With her star on the rise, she is poised for continued success and is undoubtedly a name to watch in the music industry.

item.title: Deepa Miriam
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Deepa Miriam

Playback Female Singer

Deepa Miriam is an Indian playback singer of South Indian movies. Her debut film was Naan Avanillai. Deepa rose to fame with the song Kangal Iraandal in the Tamil movie Subramaniapuram.

 

Deepa was born and brought up in the United Arab Emirates (U.A.E.), to a Malayalee Christian family, and completed schooling there. She began singing at a very young age. She received training in carnatic music, beginning at age seven. She has won first place in singing competitions in light music, semi-classical and classical categories, and performed many live music shows with musicians from Kerala when still in school. Deepa passed the Twelfth Board Exam with Distinction. She received her B. Tech. degree in Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering from Model Engineering College, Thrikkakara, Kerala.

 

After completing her education, Deepa moved to Chennai to pursue a career in playback singing. She made her debut in 2008 with the song "Unnai Nambiren" from the film Naan Avanillai. She has since sung for over 50 films in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada. She has won several awards for her singing, including the Filmfare Award for Best Female Playback Singer – Tamil in 2010 for the song "Kangal Iraandal" from the film Subramaniapuram.

 

Deepa is a versatile singer with a wide range of vocal abilities. She is known for her soulful renditions of both classical and contemporary songs. She is also a popular live performer and has performed at several concerts in India and abroad.

item.title: Deepali Sahay
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Deepali Sahay

Playback Female Singer

Deepali Sahay is an Indian singer who gained recognition through her participation in the reality singing competition Indian Idol. She rose to prominence as a finalist in Indian Idol Season 3, showcasing her exceptional vocal abilities and captivating performances.

 

Following her success on Indian Idol, Deepali Sahay continued to make her mark in the industry. In Indian Idol Season 4, she expanded her skills by co-hosting the auditions and the Roobaroos segment alongside Meiyang Chang. Her charming personality and rapport with contestants added an engaging element to the show.

 

Deepali Sahay further extended her presence in the music industry as she co-hosted the music show Bharat Ki Shaan: Singing Star on DD National. Alongside Abhas Joshi, she brought her talent and charisma to the show, showcasing her versatility and ability to connect with the audience.

 

Throughout her career, Deepali Sahay has demonstrated her passion and dedication to music. Her journey from being a finalist in Indian Idol to taking on hosting roles highlights her versatility as an artist. She continues to leave a lasting impact with her soulful voice and magnetic stage presence.

With her musical talent and on-screen charm, Deepali Sahay has garnered a strong fan base and earned respect from industry professionals. Her contributions to the entertainment industry have solidified her position as a prominent figure in the music and television domains.

 

In summary, Deepali Sahay is a talented Indian singer who gained fame as a finalist in Indian Idol Season 3. Her involvement in subsequent seasons and hosting roles on shows like Bharat Ki Shaan: Singing Star have further showcased her versatility and appeal. With her remarkable vocal abilities and engaging personality, Deepali Sahay continues to enthrall audiences and leave a lasting impression in the industry.

item.title: Dhvani Bhanushali
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Dhvani Bhanushali

Playback Female Singer

Dhvani Bhanushali is a talented Indian singer and songwriter who has made a notable impact on the Indian music industry. Born on June 22, 1998, in Mumbai, India, Dhvani gained widespread recognition and popularity at a young age.

 

Dhvani's musical journey began in 2017 when she released her debut single "Ishtehaar" for the Bollywood film "Welcome to New York." However, it was her second single, "Dilbar," a remake of a classic Bollywood song, that catapulted her to stardom. The song became a massive hit and garnered millions of views, making Dhvani a household name overnight.

 

Known for her versatile vocal range and soothing voice, Dhvani continued to deliver hit after hit. Some of her popular songs include "Vaaste," "Leja Re," "Na Ja Tu," and "Psycho Saiyaan," among others. Her melodious voice and captivating performances have earned her a dedicated fan base and critical acclaim.

 

Dhvani has collaborated with several renowned artists and musicians in the industry, showcasing her versatility and ability to adapt to different genres and styles. Her songs often blend elements of pop, romantic ballads, and peppy dance numbers, making her music appealing to a wide audience.

In addition to her singing career, Dhvani has also received accolades for her live performances, mesmerizing audiences with her stage presence and energy. She has been honored with awards such as the Mirchi Music Awards and the Global Indian Music Academy Awards for her exceptional contributions to the music industry.

item.title: Falguni Pathak
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Falguni Pathak

Playback Female Singer

Falguni Pathak  (born 12 March 1971) is an Indian singer, performing artist  and composer based in mumbai . Her music is based on traditional musical forms from the Indian state of gujurat. Since her professional debut in 1987, she has developed into an artist with a large fan base across India. Once asked how she decided to take up singing as a career, she replied that it happened by default.

 

Her debut album was released in 1998, and she has also recorded numerous songs for bollywood  movies. The theme of most of her songs is love. She has performed in many shows in India and other countries, backed by a band called Tha Thaiyaa. 

 

she has some very popular indian pop singles to her credit, still heard and appreciated all over India. Her albums are not only famous for the melodious songs but also for the cute love stories depicted with them. She is very popular with the gujurati community where she is called to perform for popular festivals like navarati

 

Some of her popular songs are Chudi Jo Khanki Haathon Mein, Maine Payal Hai Chhankai, Meri Chunar Udd Udd Jaye, Ayi Pardesh Se Pariyon Ki Rani and Sawaan Mein.

 

Falguni Pathak's mesmerizing voice, combined with her vibrant stage presence and ability to connect with her audience, has made her an iconic figure in the realm of Gujarati folk music and the Navratri festival. Her influence continues to inspire and entertain music lovers, ensuring her place as one of the most beloved singers in India.

she has some very popular indian pop singles to her credit, still heard and appreciated all over India. item.title: Geeta Rabari
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Geeta Rabari

Playback Female Singer

Geeta Rabari is a popular Gujarati folk singer from India who gained widespread recognition for her powerful vocals and energetic performances. She is known for her soulful renditions of traditional folk songs and her contributions to the Gujarati music industry. Geeta Rabari was born on December 31, 1996, in Tappar village, Kutch district, Gujarat. She developed a passion for music at a young age and started singing at local cultural events and religious gatherings. Her talent was soon discovered by music producers, leading her to embark on a professional singing career. 

 

Known for her distinctive voice and energetic performances, Geeta Rabari has captivated audiences with her charismatic stage presence. Her lively and engaging style, coupled with her powerful vocals, has made her a favorite among Gujarati music lovers.

 

Geeta Rabari's songs are often characterized by their catchy beats, folk-inspired melodies, and meaningful lyrics that reflect the joys, sorrows, and aspirations of rural life. Her music resonates with a wide range of listeners, transcending boundaries and appealing to people from different backgrounds.

item.title: Geetha Madhuri
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Geetha Madhuri

Playback Female Singer

Geetha Madhuri is an Indian playback singer and voice artist. She has sung over 1800 songs in several languages including Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam. She is a recepeint of numerous Nandi Awards and Filmfare awards.

 

Geetha was born to Prabhakar Sastry, a State Bank of India official, and Lakshmi. Madhuri is their only daughter. Her family moved from Palakollu, West Godavari District to Hyderabad when she was very young. Madhuri was schooled at Loyala Model High School, Vanasthalipuram and Little Flower Junior College. She graduated in B Com at Aurora College. She was trained in classical and light music by Kocharlakota Padmavati and Ramachari. Madhuri made her debut as a playback singer with Kulasekhar's film Premalekha Rasa. Madhuri married actor Nandu in 2014. The couple have a daughter born in 2019 named Dakshayani Prakruthi.

 

Geetha has sung for some of the biggest names in the Telugu film industry, including Mahesh Babu, Pawan Kalyan, Allu Arjun, Ram Charan, and Jr NTR. She has also sung for some of the biggest names in the Tamil film industry, including Vijay, Ajith Kumar, Suriya, and Dhanush.

 

Geetha is a versatile singer with a wide range of vocal abilities. She is known for her soulful renditions of both classical and contemporary songs. She is also a popular live performer and has performed at several concerts in India and abroad.

item.content:encoded:
Himani Kapoor

Playback Female Singer

Himani Kapoor is an Indian singer and finalist of Sa Re Ga Ma PA challenge 2005. She also hosted a show with karan oberoi on Zee Tv called "Antakshari". She also competed in Star Plus's jo jeeta wahi sikhander She gained wider recognition for singing song in pagglait called "Thode Kam Ajnabi" composed by Arijit singh .

 

She has sung in , Dil Diya Hai, Aap Ki Khatir, Chingari, Bachna Ae Haseeno, Fool N Final, Oye Lucky! Lucky Oye! and Band Baaja Baaraat.

 

She released a song dedicated to indira gandhi on the occasion of women's day in 2010.

item.title: Harshdeep Kaur
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Harshdeep Kaur

Playback Female Singer

Harshdeep Kaur is a talented Indian singer known for her soulful voice and versatility across various genres. Born on December 16, 1986, in Delhi, India, Harshdeep began her musical journey at a young age and has since become a prominent figure in the Indian music industry

Known for her proficiency in Sufi and Punjabi folk music, Harshdeep has carved a niche for herself in the industry. She has lent her enchanting voice to numerous Bollywood film songs, including "Katiya Karoon" from the film "Rockstar," "Heer" from "Jab Tak Hai Jaan," and "Dilbaro" from "Raazi," among others. Her evocative renditions and emotive singing style have won her a dedicated fan base.

In addition to Bollywood, Harshdeep has also collaborated with various renowned artists and musicians, both in India and internationally. She has showcased her versatility by exploring different genres, including pop, fusion, and devotional music. Her collaborations with artists like A.R. Rahman, Shankar Mahadevan, and Pritam have received critical acclaim.

Harshdeep's talent has been recognized with several prestigious awards, including the National Film Award for Best Female Playback Singer and the Filmfare Award for Best Female Playback Singer.

Ishita Vishwakarma

Playback Female Singer

Ishita Vishwakarma is a singer who was born on May 10, 2002, in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. She is currently around 20 years old as of 2022 and her zodiac sign is Taurus.

 

Ishita received her early music education from her parents and later pursued formal training in music at the Divisional Bal Bhavan in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, under the guidance of Indian music guru Dr. Shipra Sullere. She further continued her training under the mentorship of Indian music guru Prakash Virunkar.

item.title: Jyotica Tangri
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Jyotica Tangri

Playback Female Singer

Jyotica Tangri is an Indian playback singer who has sung for many Bollywood films. She made her debut with the song "Phir Bhi Tumko Chaahungi" from the film Half Girlfriend (2017), but her version was not included in the film. Shraddha Kapoor's version of the song became a hit. She has since sung for films like Behen Hogi Teri (2017), Shaadi Mein Zaroor Aana (2017), Fukrey Returns (2017), Parmanu: The Story of Pokhran (2018), and Virgin Bhanupriya (2020). In 2018, she won the Zee Cine Award for Best Female Playback Singer for her song "Shubh Din" from Parmanu: The Story of Pokhran. She made her Punjabi debut with the song "Bajre Da Sitta" in 2021.

 

Here is a list of some of Jyotica Tangri's most popular songs:

  • "Phir Bhi Tumko Chaahungi" (Half Girlfriend)
  • "Khadke Glassy" (Shaadi Mein Zaroor Aana)
  • "Ishq De Fanniyar" (Fukrey Returns)
  • "Shubh Din" (Parmanu: The Story of Pokhran)
  • "Bajre Da Sitta" (Punjabi)

June Banerjee 

Playback Female Singer

june banerjee  is a talented singer who has sung in a number of films and ad jingles. She is known for her beautiful voice and her ability to sing in a variety of languages. Some of her most popular songs include "Soniye Tu Janiye Tu, Laila Laila" and "Kehna Hai Kehna Hai."

 

June Banerjee was born in Kolkata, India. She started singing at a young age and quickly developed a love for music. She studied music at the University of Calcutta and later moved to Mumbai to pursue a career in playback singing.

 

June Banerjee made her playback singing debut in the 2008 film Chirodini Tumi Je Amar. She has since sung in a number of other films, including Khokababu, Lorai, and Moner Manush. She has also sung in a number of ad jingles for brands such as Pepsi, Coca-Cola, and Fair & Lovely.

item.title: Jonita Gandhi
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Jonita Gandhi

Playback Female Singer

Jonita Gandhi is a Canadian playback singer of Indian descent. She has recorded songs predominantly in Hindi and Tamil languages with few in Punjabi, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali, Kannada and Malayalam languages. Some of her most acclaimed songs include The Breakup Song, Mental Manadhil, Chellama and Arabic Kuthu. She is also well known for her YouTube presence. Her singing debut started through Chennai Express title track (in 2013).

 

Gandhi was born in a Punjabi family from Delhi. Her family emigrated to Brampton, Canada when she was nine months old, where she was raised. Her family later settled in Mississauga.

 

Gandhi studied in Turner Fenton Secondary School and attended the Ivey Business School of the University of Western Ontario where she completed her degrees in health science and business in 2012. She has had formal training in Western and Hindustani classical singing.

 

Gandhi grew up around music as both her father and brother were part time musicians. They would often perform cover songs together at live community events. At age 16, she auditioned for Canadian Idol but didn't get past the audition rounds. She began making YouTube covers from her bedroom, sometimes featuring other local musicians including Akash Gandhi. The videos quickly went viral and led to a myriad of opportunities to perform. Her hits on YouTube began with covers of well-known Hindi-film songs, such as, Pani Da Rang, Tujhko Jo Paaya, Tum Hi Ho, Suhaani Raat, Yeh Honsla and many others. Her beginning concerts typically consisted of these covers.

Her jump to playback singing began with an opportunity to perform alongside Sonu Nigam. This tour crossed various countries including Russia, UK, US and the Caribbean. Afterwards, her sights were set on starting a career in the Bollywood music industry. Gandhi started playback singing with Chennai Express. The music for this film was composed by Vishal–Shekhar. She further worked in other Bollywood movies like Highway, singing both Kahaan Hoon Main and Implosive Silence.

Gandhi worked as a playback singer with music directors including A. R. Rahman and Pritam. Rahman featured Gandhi in the concert film One Heart (film). Gandhi performed at the 2016 Jubilee Games in Dubai with Salim–Sulaiman and with Amit Trivedi on MTV Unplugged.

Gandhi has also released a number of independent singles, including "The Breakup Song", which became a massive hit on YouTube and other streaming platforms. She has also collaborated with international artists such as Jason Derulo and Zara Larsson.

item.title: Jannabi Das
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Jannabi Das

Playback Female Singer

Jannabi Das, a remarkable singer hailing from the vibrant Indian Idol Season 11, has left an indelible mark on the hearts of music enthusiasts across the nation. With her soulful voice and captivating performances, Jannabi mesmerized both the judges and the audience throughout the entire season.

Born with an inherent talent for music, Jannabi effortlessly showcased her versatility by effortlessly traversing various genres, including classical, Bollywood, and contemporary pop. Her mellifluous vocals possessed an ethereal quality that effortlessly conveyed emotions, leaving listeners spellbound.

Throughout her journey on Indian Idol, Jannabi consistently demonstrated her exceptional vocal range, impeccable control, and remarkable stage presence. She had an innate ability to connect with her audience, transcending barriers and touching the hearts of millions. Her performances were characterized by an effortless grace and a unique blend of passion and vulnerability.

Jannabi's talent, coupled with her relentless dedication and perseverance, earned her accolades from the esteemed panel of judges and catapulted her to the top ranks of the competition. Her flawless renditions of iconic melodies and her ability to infuse her own style into every performance made her a fan favorite.

item.title: Jasmine Sandlas
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Jasmine Sandlas

Playback Female Singer

Jasmine Sandlas is an Indian-American singer, rapper, television personality, performer, and songwriter who mainly sings punjabi  songs. She was also featured on the Tedx Talks, MTV coke studio and spoken word platforms. Jasmine Sandlas is an independent artist.

Sandlas, born in Jalandar, Punjab, India and raised in Stockton, California always aspired to pursue a career in singing.

Sandlas' first song was "Muskan" (2008) became a hit. In 2014, she began her Bollywood playback singing career with the song "Yaar Na Miley" for the film kick . Upon its release, "Yaar Na Miley" went viral and topped the charts and Sandlas received wide critical acclaim for her singing style as well as earned several awards, including "Most popular song of year 2016 - PTC punjab film awards" and screen award for best female playback .

Moreover, she is also known as the Queen of Punjabi music industry among her fans due to her unique style of singing and lifestyle.

She was only 16 when she began writing songs.

Sandlas has since released several albums and singles, including "Patt Lai Geya", "Dil Tutteya", and "Jee Jeha Karda". She has also collaborated with some of the biggest names in Punjabi music, including Gippy Grewal, Diljit Dosanjh, and Badshah.

Sandlas is a talented singer and songwriter who has made a name for herself in the Punjabi music industry. She is known for her powerful voice and her ability to connect with her audience. She is a popular choice for playback singing and has sung for some of the biggest names in Punjabi music. She is also a talented live performer and has performed in front of large audiences all over the world.

item.title: Jaspinder Narula
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Jaspinder Narula

Playback Female Singer

Jaspinder Narula is an Indian singer known for her contributions to playback, classical, and Sufi music in both Hindi and Punjabi cinema. She was born on November 14, 1970. One of her notable achievements was winning the 1999 Filmfare Award for Best Female Playback Singer for the duet "Pyaar To Hona Hi Tha" with Remo Fernandes from the film Pyaar To Hona Hi Tha (1998).

 

Throughout her career, Jaspinder Narula has sung in various popular films, including Mission Kashmir, Mohabbatein, Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani, and Bunty Aur Babli. She has also ventured into Sufi music and sung Gurbani and other Sikh religious music. In recent years, she collaborated with Mudasir Ali on the Hindi music video "Maula Ali Ali."

 

In 2008, Jaspinder Narula participated in and won the title of India's Best Live Performer in the NDTV Imagine singing reality series, Dhoom Macha De.

 

Her musical journey began at an early age, influenced by her father, Kesar Singh Narula, who was a music composer of the 1950s. She received training from her father and Ustad Ghulam Sadiq Khan of Rampur Sahaswan Gharana. Initially, she focused on singing bhajans and Sufi compositions before transitioning to film singing. Her breakthrough came when music director Viju Shah, son of Kalyanji, gave her a break in films like Master, Aar Ya Paar, and Bade Miyan Chhote Miyan in 1998.

 

Jaspinder Narula has recorded numerous music albums and lent her voice to many successful Bollywood films, including Dulhe Raja, Virasat, Mission Kashmir, Mohabbatein, and Bunty Aur Babli.

 

On a personal note, she resides in Mumbai and is married to a Canada-based Indian businessman. She completed her schooling at Guru Harkishan Public School in India Gate, New Delhi. She pursued a B.A. (Hons) in Music from Indraprastha College for Women, where she was admitted as a special case since Music was not a subject in her 12th-grade curriculum, which was a prerequisite for the course. She also earned a Ph.D. in Hindustani classical music from Delhi University in 2008.

Jaspinder Narula is an Indian singer known for her contributions to playback, classical, and Sufi music in both Hindi and Punjabi cinema. She was born on November 14, 1970. One of her notable achievements was winning the 1999 Filmfare Award for Best Female Playback Singer for the duet \"Pyaar To Hona Hi Tha\" with Remo Fernandes from the film Pyaar To Hona Hi Tha (1998).<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Throughout her career, Jaspinder Narula has sung in various popular films, including Mission Kashmir, Mohabbatein, Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani, and Bunty Aur Babli. She has also ventured into Sufi music and sung Gurbani and other Sikh religious music. In recent years, she collaborated with Mudasir Ali on the Hindi music video \"Maula Ali Ali.\"<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

In 2008, Jaspinder Narula participated in and won the title of India's Best Live Performer in the NDTV Imagine singing reality series, Dhoom Macha De.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Her musical journey began at an early age, influenced by her father, Kesar Singh Narula, who was a music composer of the 1950s. She received training from her father and Ustad Ghulam Sadiq Khan of Rampur Sahaswan Gharana. Initially, she focused on singing bhajans and Sufi compositions before transitioning to film singing. Her breakthrough came when music director Viju Shah, son of Kalyanji, gave her a break in films like Master, Aar Ya Paar, and Bade Miyan Chhote Miyan in 1998.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Jaspinder Narula has recorded numerous music albums and lent her voice to many successful Bollywood films, including Dulhe Raja, Virasat, Mission Kashmir, Mohabbatein, and Bunty Aur Babli.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

On a personal note, she resides in Mumbai and is married to a Canada-based Indian businessman. She completed her schooling at Guru Harkishan Public School in India Gate, New Delhi. She pursued a B.A. (Hons) in Music from Indraprastha College for Women, where she was admitted as a special case since Music was not a subject in her 12th-grade curriculum, which was a prerequisite for the course. She also earned a Ph.D. in Hindustani classical music from Delhi University in 2008.<\/p>","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_weight":"bold"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":false}],"isInner":false},{"id":"f0add38","elType":"section","settings":{"background_background":"classic","background_color":"#EAF0EE8F","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"ac4fb18"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"a1b2b38"}]},"elements":[{"id":"3c321e6","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":100,"_inline_size":null},"elements":[{"id":"a125bcd","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Enquiry Form","header_size":"h3","align":"center","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_size":{"unit":"px","size":40,"sizes":[]},"typography_font_weight":"bold","_margin":{"unit":"px","top":"40","right":"0","bottom":"20","left":"0","isLinked":false},"__globals__":{"title_color":"globals\/colors?id=6d3d44f9"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"},{"id":"1c1fef0","elType":"widget","settings":{"shortcode":"[forminator_form id=\"5483\"]","_margin":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"40","left":"0","isLinked":false}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"shortcode"}],"isInner":false}],"isInner":false}]

item.title: Kavya Limaye
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Kavya Limaye

Playback Female Singer

Kavya Limaye, a talented singer from Indian Idol, has captivated audiences with her soulful voice and magnetic stage presence. Hailing from a small town, Kavya's journey to the Indian Idol stage is nothing short of inspiring. Her melodic renditions and impeccable control over her vocals have won the hearts of both the judges and viewers.

With each performance, Kavya showcases her versatility by effortlessly switching genres, be it classical, Bollywood, or contemporary hits. Her ability to connect with the emotions of a song and deliver it with utmost authenticity sets her apart as a remarkable performer. Kavya's vocal range and flawless technique leave a lasting impact on anyone who witnesses her powerful performances.

Beyond her musical abilities, Kavya exudes humility and grace, making her an instant favorite among fans. Her dedication, hard work, and determination to pursue her passion have made her an inspiration for aspiring singers across the nation. As Kavya Limaye continues to shine on the Indian Idol stage, she is undoubtedly on the path to becoming a prominent figure in the Indian music industry.

item.title: Khushboo Grewal
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Khushboo Grewal

Playback Female Singer

Khushboo Grewal, also known as Khushboo Kochhar, is an Indian playback singer and actress. She began her career as a VJ on B4U channel and later ventured into Punjabi and Hindi films as an actor. While she has appeared in movies like "Raaz: The Mystery Continues" and Punjabi films such as "Carry on Jatta," she is primarily recognized as a playback singer.

 

Khushboo gained prominence for her rendition of the song "Pink Lips," composed by Meet Bros, from the Bollywood movie "Hate Story 2." She is also the lead vocalist of the Meet Bros band, showcasing her musical talents.

 

Born into a family of doctors, Khushboo graduated from MCM DAV College for Women in Chandigarh. In 2006, she married entrepreneur Bipin Grewal, and the couple has a daughter named Shanaya.

 

Khushboo initially started her entertainment career as a VJ, where she had the opportunity to interview well-known Bollywood celebrities. She has also acted in Punjabi films such as "Munde U.K. De," "Carry On Jatta," and "Bhaji in Problem." Additionally, she has appeared in TV serials like "Dil Dosti Dance," "Rang Badalti Odhani," and "Chajje Chajje Ka Pyaar."

 

As a singer, Khushboo began her journey with the title track of the 2013 film "Boss" as a backing vocalist. However, she gained fame with her song "Pink Lips" from "Hate Story 2." Some of her other notable songs include "Selfiyaan" from "Sharafat Gayi Tel Lene," "Lak Tunu Tunu" from "Double Di Trouble," "Tu Takke" from "Dharam Sankat Mein," and "Awesome Mora Mahiya" from "Calendar Girls."

item.title: Kinjal Dave
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Kinjal Dave

Playback Female Singer

Kinjal Dave is a popular Gujarati folk and playback singer from India. She gained widespread recognition for her performances in traditional Garba and Dandiya events, as well as her contributions to Gujarati film and music industry.

Kinjal Dave was born on November 24, 1999, in the small village of Patan, Gujarat, India. She developed a passion for music at a young age and started performing at local cultural events and weddings. Her talent soon caught the attention of music producers, leading to her professional singing career.

In 2016, Kinjal Dave gained immense popularity with her hit song "Char Bangdi Vali Gadi." The song went viral on social media platforms and became a sensation, earning her widespread acclaim and establishing her as a prominent name in the Gujarati music industry. Since then, she has released numerous successful singles, including "Leri Lala," "Chote Raja," and "DJ Jonadiyo Part 3," among others.

Apart from her independent music career, Kinjal Dave has also lent her voice to Gujarati films. She has sung playback tracks for movies like "Vijay Suvada Ni Dikri No.1," "Janu Mari Jaan," and "Preet Janmo Janam Ni Bhulase Nahi."

Kinjal Dave's energetic and soulful performances have made her a favorite among Gujarati music lovers. Her songs are known for their catchy beats, folk-inspired melodies, and vibrant lyrics. She continues to release new music and perform at various events, captivating audiences with her talent and charisma.

item.title: Lisa Mishra
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Lisa Mishra

Playback Female Singer

Lisa Mishra is a talented singer who has captivated audiences with her soulful voice and mesmerizing performances. Born and raised in Chicago, Lisa has successfully bridged the gap between Indian and Western music, creating a unique and refreshing sound that resonates with listeners of all backgrounds. Her journey to stardom began when she uploaded a cover of the popular Bollywood song "Tareefan" on YouTube, which quickly went viral and caught the attention of music industry professionals.

Since then, Lisa has collaborated with renowned artists and composers, and has released several hit singles, including "Nai Chaida" and "Tera Ban Jaunga." Her music is characterized by its rich melodies, heartfelt lyrics, and a perfect blend of Indian classical and contemporary pop elements. Lisa's versatility as a singer allows her to effortlessly transition between different genres, captivating listeners with her expressive vocals and innate musicality.

With her infectious energy and genuine passion for music, Lisa Mishra has earned a dedicated fan base and continues to enchant audiences with her soul-stirring performances. item.title: Madhushree
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Madhushree

Playback Female Singer

Madhushree, originally named Sujata Bhattacharya, is an Indian playback singer known for her work in Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, Kannada, and Telugu films. She was born on November 2, 1969, in Kolkata, India. Coming from a musically inclined family, Madhushree received her initial training in classical and western styles of music from her parents, Amarendranath and Parbati Bhattacharya, who were also her first teachers. She further pursued her musical education at Rabindra Bharati University, where she completed her master's degree. While her father aspired for her to become a classical singer, Madhushree's true passion lay in becoming a playback singer.

 

During her early years, Madhushree worked for the Indian Council for Cultural Relations and was deputed to teach classical music in Suriname. However, her ultimate goal was to establish a career in the playback singing industry, which led her to move to Mumbai.

 

In her pursuit of a breakthrough, Madhushree recorded her music on CDs and sent them to prominent individuals in Bollywood. One of these CDs reached Javed Akhtar, a renowned lyricist, who recommended her for opportunities. This led to her playback singing debut in Rajesh Roshan's film "Moksha." Following her debut, she went on to lend her voice to songs in movies such as "Yuva," "Aayitha Ezhuthu," "Kal Ho Naa Ho," and "Kuch Naa Kaho." Madhushree has had a fruitful collaboration with the acclaimed composer A. R. Rahman, singing memorable songs like "Tu Bin Bataye," "In Lamhon Ke Daaman Me," and "Ham Hain Ispal Yahan."

 

In the film "Tehzeeb," composed by A. R. Rahman, Madhushree sang three songs and was credited as Sujata Bhattacharya. She gained recognition for her rendition of "Kabhi Neem Neem" from the movie "Yuva" (2004) and received the prestigious Sony Stardust Award for Best Female Sensation (Playback Singer). Madhushree's repertoire also includes the song "In Lamhon Ke Daaman Mein" from the film "Jodhaa Akbar," composed by A. R. Rahman, and "Soja Zara" from "Bahubali 2 – The Conclusion." Her exceptional contributions to the music industry have earned her accolades, including the Lions Gold Award for All-Time Film Versatile Playback Singer at the 20th edition of the ceremony held at Bhaidas Hall in Mumbai.

item.title: Maitrayee Patar
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Maitrayee Patar

Playback Female Singer

Maitrayee Patar is an Indian writer, poet, and musical artist from Assam. She is best known for her contributions to Assamese literature and new-age music.

 

Born on April 7, 1990, in Guwahati, Maitrayee Patar belongs to the Tiwa community, which is an indigenous tribal community. She completed her post-graduation in Sociology from the Delhi School of Economics and further pursued a Master of Philosophy in Women's Studies from the Tata Institute of Social Sciences in Mumbai.

 

In the field of literature, Maitrayee Patar has authored a poetry book titled "Mor Kolmou Dinor Xonali Baat," published in 2015. Her poetry often explores and reflects upon the natural world and the lives of women. Her poems have been translated into various Indian and foreign languages, including Italian, Tiwa, Nepali, Hindi, and Malayalam. She is a regular contributor to esteemed literary magazines such as Krittibas, Satsori, Prakash, Nebedan, and Jatra.

 

Maitrayee Patar is also involved in the realm of music, particularly in the genre of new-age music. She is associated with the music label Baartalaap. Her alternative rock song "Dur Ximonat" gained recognition and was featured in Rolling Stone India's first playlist of 2020.

item.title: Malavika
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Malavika

Playback Female Singer

Malavika is a popular Tollywood playback singer known for her work in the Telugu film industry. She began her singing career with the song "Nuvvu nenu kalisunte" for the movie Gangotri. With her versatile voice, she has sung for around 500 movies to date and has received accolades, including Nandi Awards for Best Playback Singer in 2006 and 2011.

 

Malavika's talent was evident from a young age, and she was the winner of ETV Padutha Teeyaga as a child. She continues to showcase her singing abilities on shows like ETV Swarabhishekam and MAATV Super Singer series 7, 8, and 9.

Some of Malavika's hit songs include "Bommali" from the movie Billa, "Amma avani" from Rajanna, "Sunday Monday" from Khaleja, "Vennelaina cheekataina" from Prema Katta Chitram, and "Holessa" from Sri Ramadasu. Apart from Telugu, she has also lent her voice to songs in Kannada and Hindi. Her first song was actually an English song for the movie Rockford, followed by a Hindi song for Bollywood Calling.

 

Malavika received her initial training in music from her mother, who herself is a radio artist and singer. She then received classical training from Kum Mandapaka Sarada. She completed her schooling at Little Angels High School in MVP Colony, Visakhapatnam, where her mother taught music. After gaining popularity in the film industry, Malavika and her family relocated to Hyderabad.

 

Known for her distinctive voice and dedication, Malavika is highly regarded as a hard-working artist. Music directors have praised her for her cooperation and willingness to sing numerous times to achieve the desired result.

item.title: Mamta Joshi
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Mamta Joshi

Playback Female Singer

Mamta Joshi is a renowned Sufi singer whose melodious voice and soulful renditions have captivated audiences worldwide. Born with a natural talent for singing, she has dedicated her life to the art of Sufi music, mesmerizing listeners with her heartfelt performances.

 

Mamta Joshi's unique ability lies in her ability to convey the profound spiritual essence of Sufi poetry through her voice. With every note she sings, she effortlessly transports her listeners into a realm of spiritual transcendence, evoking emotions of love, devotion, and longing for the divine.

 

Her impeccable control over her vocal range, coupled with her deep understanding of Sufi philosophy and traditions, has earned her a special place in the hearts of music enthusiasts. Mamta Joshi's mastery over various Sufi musical genres, including Qawwali, Ghazal, and Kafi, showcases her versatility as an artist.

 

Beyond her musical talents, Mamta Joshi is admired for her humility and dedication to her craft. She continues to inspire aspiring singers and Sufi music lovers with her timeless melodies, reminding us of the transformative power of music on the human soul.

item.title: Mamta Sharma
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Mamta Sharma

Playback Female Singer

Mamta Sharma is an Indian playback singer known for her contributions to the music industry. She gained widespread recognition for her song "Munni Badnaam Hui" from the film Dabangg and "Tinku Jiya" from Yamla Pagla Deewana. Both songs became chartbusters and earned her numerous awards and nominations, including a Filmfare award for Best Playback Singer (Female).

 

Born in Birla Nagar, Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, Mamta Sharma completed her studies at Saint Paul's School in Morar, Gwalior. She displayed a passion for performing on stage during her school years and actively participated in various events. She also performed with her band at family functions such as marriage receptions and parties.

 

Before venturing into Bollywood and Bengali music, Mamta Sharma lent her voice to many Bhojpuri albums. It was music director Lalit Pandit who discovered her talent and gave her a breakthrough opportunity in the hit movie Dabangg, where she sang the popular item song "Munni Badnaam Hui." She also lent her voice to the song "Kevvu Keka" in the Telugu remake of Dabangg titled Gabbar Singh. Mamta Sharma went on to deliver other hit songs like "Fevicol Se" and "Tooh" in subsequent projects.

item.title: Mauli Dave
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Mauli Dave

Playback Female Singer

Mauli Dave, born on June 3, 1987, is a multi-talented Indian singer, actress, dancer, and television host. She gained recognition as a contestant on Zee TV's popular music reality show, "Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Challenge 2007."

Mauli's journey in the entertainment industry began earlier when she participated in Sony Entertainment's "Chalo America Boogie Woogie" in 2004, where she reached the finals. She also won the title of Miss Teen India Texas in 2007, showcasing her versatility and talent.

After her achievements in the United States, Mauli decided to move to Mumbai at the age of 19 to pursue a career in music and acting. She hosted the family dance show "Rock n Roll Family" on the Zee Network in 2008, further showcasing her hosting skills.

In the acting realm, Mauli took on a lead role in the Zoom Tele-Film "Ek Anhonee." She also participated in Fear Factor India: Khatron Ke Khiladi season 4, where she emerged as the Runner-up, demonstrating her courage and determination.

Mauli Dave hails from Gujarat, India, and has made notable appearances in various television shows and serials. She was seen in an episode of the Zee TV serial "Parrivaar," adding to her acting repertoire.

During her stint on "Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Challenge 2007," Mauli represented the United States after going through several rounds of auditions. Mentored by Bappi Lahiri, she showcased her vocal prowess with her famous rendition of the song "Mayya Mayya." Mauli's talent and dedication led her to reach the top 10 in the competition.

item.title: Meghna Mishra
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Meghna Mishra

Playback Female Singer

Meghna Mishra is an Indian playback singer known for her association with music director Amit Trivedi. She gained widespread recognition with her performances in the 2017 film Secret Superstar, where she delivered two superhit tracks, "Nachdi Phira" and "Main Kaun Hoon". The film starred Zaira Wasim, Meher Vij, and Aamir Khan.

 

Her song "Nachdi Phira" earned her the prestigious Best Female Playback Singer award at the 63rd Filmfare Awards. The track received immense acclaim for Meghna's soulful rendition and was hailed as one of the standout songs of the film. It showcased her versatility and ability to evoke emotions through her powerful vocals.

 

Another popular song from the film, "Main Kaun Hoon," was widely appreciated and resonated with the audience. It was included in the list of best Hindi songs of 2017 by an online portal. Composed by Amit Trivedi and with lyrics penned by Kausar Munir, the song showcased Meghna's ability to capture the essence of the character and deliver a heartfelt performance.

 

Meghna Mishra's association with Amit Trivedi has proven to be a successful collaboration, with her soul-stirring voice bringing life to his compositions. Her performances in Secret Superstar showcased her talent and garnered her critical acclaim. She captivated listeners with her ability to express a range of emotions through her vocals, leaving a lasting impact on the audience.

 

As a young and promising playback singer, Meghna Mishra has established herself as a versatile artist, capable of delivering captivating performances. Her success in Secret Superstar has opened doors for further opportunities in the music industry, and she continues to be recognized for her talent and contribution to Indian playback singing.

item.title: Mekhla Dasgupta
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Mekhla Dasgupta

Playback Female Singer

Mekhla Dasgupta is a talented singer who has captivated audiences with her soulful voice and dynamic performances. Hailing from a musical family, Mekhla's passion for singing developed at a young age, and she has since become a rising star in the music industry.

 

Known for her versatility, Mekhla effortlessly navigates various genres, including Indian classical, semi-classical, ghazals, and Bollywood music. Her ability to infuse emotions into her renditions leaves listeners spellbound, and her flawless vocal control showcases her immense talent.

 

Mekhla's stage presence is magnetic, and her ability to connect with her audience creates an unforgettable experience. With her charismatic personality and engaging performances, she has gained a loyal fan base that eagerly awaits her every musical endeavor.

 

In addition to her live performances, Mekhla has also made a name for herself in the recording industry, lending her voice to numerous soundtracks and albums. Her melodious collaborations with renowned composers and musicians have garnered critical acclaim and further solidified her position as a versatile vocalist.

 

With her dedication, talent, and undeniable passion for music, Mekhla Dasgupta continues to mesmerize audiences and carve her own unique path in the world of singing.

Mismi Bose

Playback Female Singer

Mismi Bose, an exceptionally talented singer, has captured the hearts of music enthusiasts around the world with her mesmerizing voice and soulful performances. With a vocal range that effortlessly traverses various genres, including classical, pop, and Bollywood, Mismi has proven to be a versatile artist, capable of creating magic with every note she sings.

 

Her voice, rich in texture and emotive depth, has the power to evoke a myriad of emotions within listeners, transporting them to a realm of pure musical bliss. Mismi's impeccable control over her voice allows her to effortlessly hit the highest highs and delve into the lowest lows, showcasing her remarkable vocal prowess.

 

Mismi Bose's musical journey began at an early age, and she has since honed her craft through years of dedicated practice and unwavering passion. Her dedication to her art is evident in every performance, as she captivates audiences with her flawless technique and heartfelt renditions.

 

Beyond her exceptional singing abilities, Mismi is also an accomplished songwriter, composing lyrics that resonate with authenticity and emotional depth. Her compositions touch upon themes of love, longing, and self-discovery, creating a profound connection with her listeners.

 

Mismi Bose stands as a true luminary in the music industry, leaving an indelible mark with her extraordinary talent and unwavering commitment to her art. Her celestial voice continues to inspire and uplift, making her a beloved figure among music lovers worldwide.

item.title: Monali Thakur
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Monali Thakur

Playback Female Singer

Monali Thakur, born on 3 November 1985, is an Indian singer and actress known for her work in the Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada film industries. She has received numerous awards, including a National Film Award for the song "Moh Moh Ke Dhaage" from the film "Dum Laga Ke Haisha" (2015) and a Filmfare Award for the song "Sawaar Loon" from the film "Lootera" (2013). She has also served as a judge on Zee TV's singing reality show "Sa Re Ga Ma Pa L'il Champs 2014" and as an "expert" on Colors TV's "Rising Star" for two seasons.

 

Born into a Bengali Hindu Rajput musical family in Kolkata, Thakur comes from a musical background. Her father, Shakti Thakur, was a singer and actor in the Bengali film industry, and her sister, Mehuli Thakur, is a playback singer in Bengal. Monali has learned hip-hop, Bharatanatyam, and salsa dance forms.

 

Thakur started her singing career by participating in school and college competitions and performing at local functions. In 1999, at the age of 14, she recorded the title track of the Bengali serial "Shri Ramkrishna" and received the Best Playback Singer Award at the Anandalok Awards for her performance. She gained popularity after securing the ninth position in the singing competition show "Indian Idol 2."

 

After "Indian Idol," Thakur faced challenges in establishing herself in the music industry. However, she got a breakthrough opportunity when music director Pritam Chakraborty offered her two songs for the Bollywood film "Race" in 2008, namely "Khwab Dekhe" (Sexy Lady) and "Zara Zara Touch Me." The song "Zara Zara Touch Me" became a huge success and garnered her nominations for the IIFA Award for Best Female Playback and the Apsara Award for Best Female Playback Singer.

 

Thakur's singing career continued to flourish, and she won the Filmfare Award for Best Female Playback Singer for the song "Sawaar Loon" from the film "Lootera" (2014). She received further acclaim, including a National Film Award for Best Female Playback Singer for the song "Moh Moh Ke Dhaage" from the film "Dum Laga Ke Haisha" (2015).

Apart from playback singing, Thakur has released several singles, including "Tamanna" (2018), "Shy Mora Saiyaan" (2018), "O Re Naseeba" (2019), "Pani Pani Re" (2019), "Dugga Elo" (2019), "Dil Ka Fitoor" (2020), and more.

In her personal life, Thakur married Maik Richter, a restaurateur based in Switzerland, in 2017. She met Richter during a backpacking trip to Switzerland, where he was her Airbnb host. Thakur publicly announced their marriage in June 2020 after releasing her single "Dil Ka Fitoor," which features her along with Maik.

item.title: Nahid Afrin
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Nahid Afrin

Playback Female Singer

Nahid Afrin is an Indian singer who gained recognition through her participation in the reality TV show "Indian Idol Junior" in 2015. She was born on December 23, 2001, in Biswanath Chariali, Assam, India.

 

Nahid's soulful voice and captivating performances during her time on "Indian Idol Junior" won the hearts of both the judges and the audience. Despite being a young contestant, she showcased remarkable talent and received praise for her versatility in singing various genres.

 

Following her appearance on the show, Nahid Afrin continued to pursue her singing career and released her debut album titled "Aye Mere Ujale Maa" in 2016. The album showcased her vocal abilities and received positive reviews.

 

Apart from her album, Nahid has also lent her voice to several film soundtracks in the Assamese film industry. Some of her notable songs include "Borgeet" from the film "Mission China" and "Bulbul" from the film "Gunjan".

item.title: Neelanjana Ray
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Neelanjana Ray

Playback Female Singer

Neelanjana Ray is an Indian playback singer who gained recognition through her appearances in music reality shows. She was born on November 25, 1995, in Alipurduar, West Bengal, India.

 

Neelanjana first rose to prominence when she participated in the reality singing competition "Sa Re Ga Ma Pa L'il Champs" in 2009. Her soulful and melodious voice impressed both the judges and the audience, and she emerged as one of the top contestants in the show. Her performances in the show showcased her versatility and garnered her a dedicated fan following.

 

Following her success on "Sa Re Ga Ma Pa L'il Champs," Neelanjana continued to pursue her passion for singing. She has performed in various concerts and musical events across India, captivating audiences with her powerful vocals and emotional renditions.

item.title: Neeti Mohan
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Neeti Mohan

Playback Female Singer

Neeti Mohan is an Indian singer known for her work in Hindi and Tamil films, as well as other regional languages like Marathi, Telugu, Kannada, Bengali, Punjabi, and English. She was born in Delhi on November 18, 1979. Neeti gained initial recognition by participating in the reality show "Popstars" on Channel V, where she emerged as one of the winners and became a member of the pop group Aasma, formed with other winners. She rose to prominence after recording the song "Ishq Wala Love" for the film "Student of the Year" (2012), which led to her winning the Filmfare R. D. Burman Award for New Music Talent. She was also nominated for Best Female Playback Singer for the song "Jiya Re" from "Jab Tak Hai Jaan" (2012).

 

Neeti Mohan's rendition of six jazz tracks in the soundtrack album of Amit Trivedi's "Bombay Velvet" (2015) received positive reviews from music critics. She received her second nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Female Playback Singer for the song "Sau Aasmaan" from the film "Baar Baar Dekho" (2016). In addition to her singing career, Neeti Mohan has been involved in various charities and social causes.

 

Born to P. V. Ramankutty Varier and M. T. Vijayalakshmy, Neeti Mohan is the eldest of four sisters, including Shakti Mohan, Mukti Mohan, and Kriti Mohan. She began learning music at the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya at the age of four and participated in various music contests during her school days. She was part of the school band and represented India as a Youth Exchange Programme cadet. Neeti continued her music training at the Bhatkhande Music Institute and received further training in Mumbai. She also studied dancing, including Bharata Natyam and Kathak.

Neeti Mohan gained early exposure to the music industry through her participation in "Popstars" and went on to collaborate with renowned artists like A. R. Rahman. She was part of the winning team "Shankar's Rockstars" on the Star Plus show "Music Ka Maha Muqqabla" in 2009. In terms of her personal life, Neeti Mohan married actor Nihaar Pandya on February 15, 2019, and the couple announced their first pregnancy on their second wedding anniversary in 2021.

In an interview, Neeti Mohan shared an interesting anecdote about how A. R. Rahman discovered her. Her sister Shakti was performing as a dancer at an A. R. Rahman show, and Neeti expressed her desire to speak to Rahman. Although she didn't get the chance to talk to him then, six months later, she ended up singing with him. Neeti had met Rahman's manager previously, and when she learned about auditions for Rahman's USA tour, she recorded a vocal audition and was eventually selected for the tour.

item.title: Neha Chauhan
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Neha Chauhan

Playback Female Singer

Neha Chauhan is an Indian playback singer who has made a notable impact in the music industry. With her mesmerizing voice and expressive singing style, she has garnered attention and admiration from audiences and critics alike.

Neha Chauhan has collaborated with renowned music directors and composers, lending her vocals to a diverse range of songs in various languages. Her versatility shines through as she effortlessly transitions between different genres, including romantic melodies, peppy dance tracks, and soul-stirring ballads. Her ability to convey emotions through her singing has made her a sought-after playback singer in the industry.

Known for her impeccable vocal control and range, Neha Chauhan has delivered powerful and captivating performances. Her soulful renditions have the ability to tug at the heartstrings of listeners, leaving a lasting impact. Whether it's bringing depth to a heartfelt ballad or infusing energy into a foot-tapping number, she showcases her talent and versatility with every song.

Neha Chauhan's contributions to the film industry have enriched numerous soundtracks, enhancing the storytelling and adding an extra layer of emotion. Her expressive voice brings life to the characters on screen, making the songs resonate with the audience.

Apart from her work in films, Neha Chauhan may have also lent her voice to television shows, advertisements, and private albums. Her distinct vocal timbre and ability to convey the essence of a song have made her a beloved artist in the music fraternity.

In summary, Neha Chauhan is a talented playback singer known for her versatility and captivating performances. Her expressive voice and ability to evoke emotions have made her a prominent figure in the Indian music industry. She continues to enthrall listeners with her exceptional talent and leaves a lasting impression with her soulful renditions.

item.title: Nikhita Gandhi
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Nikhita Gandhi

Playback Female Singer

Nikhita Gandhi, born on October 1, 1991, is an Indian playback singer known for her work in Indian films across multiple languages. She has lent her voice to Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Bengali, and Kannada film projects.

 

Nikhita gained recognition as the voice behind Deepika Padukone in the title track "Raabta" from the film of the same name. She has also delivered hit songs like "Ullu ka Pattha," a duet with Arijit Singh from the film "Jagga Jasoos." Her vocal contributions can be heard in films such as "Sachin: A Billion Dreams," "Chef," "Jab Harry Met Sejal," "Ittefaq," and "Cockpit," where she collaborated with Atif Aslam on the Bengali song "Mithe Alo." Other popular songs she has sung include "Aao Kabhi Haveli Pe" and "Poster Lagwa Do."

 

Nikhita Gandhi comes from a mixed Bengali and Punjabi background and grew up in Kolkata. She attended La Martiniere for Girls, Kolkata, for her schooling. She later moved to Chennai in 2010 to pursue a degree in dentistry. As a student of A.R. Rahman's K.M. College of Music and Technology, she had the opportunity to work with Rahman during an Indo-German exchange program. This led to her auditioning individually for a commercial project called "Qyuki" with Shekhar Kapur.

 

In 2012, Nikhita released a Bengali album titled "Kotha," featuring re-arranged Nazrul Geeti, songs written by renowned poet Kazi Nazrul Islam. Her breakthrough came with the song "Ladio" from Shankar's film "I" in 2015. Composed by A.R. Rahman, she recorded the song in Hindi, Telugu, and Hindi versions, earning critical acclaim.

Apart from her film projects, Nikhita has formed a band and has performed in Kerala and Kolkata. Her band consists of Sajith Sathya, Jerard Felix, Godfrey Immanuel, and Joshua Gopal.

Nikhita Gandhi's talent and versatility have been recognized with awards and nominations. She won the Best Female Playback Singer award at the Zee Cine Awards 2018 for the title track of "Raabta." She received nominations for Best Playback Singer (Female) at the 63rd Filmfare Awards for the song "Ghar" from "Jab Harry Met Sejal" and at the 3rd Filmfare Awards East for the Bengali song "Tomra Ekhono Ki" from "Meghnad Badh Rahasya." Her song "Qaafirana" from the film "Kedarnath" became a hit, and she won the Nestle Kitkat Sony Mix Audience Music Award for Best Duet for the song along with Arijit Singh. She has also released her own singles, including "Ek Do Teen" and "Madari," featuring Vishal Dadlani

item.title: Nirali Fozdar
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Nirali Fozdar

Playback Female Singer

Nirali Fozdar is a professional singer and versatile performer hailing from Ahmedabad, Gujarat. She was born on October 7, 1986, making her 34 years old as of May 2020.

 

Nirali's passion for singing started at a young age, as she began her training under her guru Devendrabhai Patni when she was just four years old. She dedicated herself to honing her skills and achieved the Visharad degree in singing while pursuing her Bachelor's in Commerce (B.Com).

 

Throughout her musical journey, Nirali received training from renowned professionals such as Aniket Khanderkar, Pandit Gautam Mukherjee, and Lt. Sandeep Satyanarayan for voice culture. She traveled frequently to Mumbai to learn from these experts.

 

However, Nirali's big break came when she participated in a popular singing reality show and reached the finals. This exposure propelled her career and helped her gain nationwide recognition as a performer and singer.

item.title: Priya Himesh
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Priya Himesh

Playback Female Singer

Priya Himesh, also known as Priya Hemesh, is an Indian playback singer known for her work in Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, and Odia films. She has contributed her vocals to over 200 songs and has collaborated with several prominent music directors including Ilaiyaraaja, Harris Jayaraj, Imman, Vijay Antony, Devi Sri Prasad, Yuvan Shankar Raja, Mani Sharma, Karthik Raja, Bharadwaj, Dhina, and many others.

Priya's journey in music began in 1989 when she started singing in light music orchestras. She has performed in more than 5000 stage shows with leading orchestras in India and overseas, showcasing her talent and captivating audiences.

In recognition of her talent, Priya Himesh received the Filmfare Awards South for her Telugu song "Ringa Ringa" from the film Aarya 2. This achievement further established her presence in the industry and showcased her ability to deliver memorable performances through her vocals.

With her versatility and collaborations with renowned music directors, Priya Himesh continues to make significant contributions to the Indian film music industry, lending her voice to a wide range of songs in different languages.

Priya Himesh

Playback Female Singer

Priya Patidar is a talented Indian singer and actress who gained recognition with her debut single "Be My Love." From a young age, she showcased her exceptional singing abilities and even won the ZEE TV Sansui Antakshari competition, further establishing her talent and passion for music.

 

Priya has lent her melodious voice to various regional films and albums in languages such as Gujarati, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Bengali. Her versatility as a singer allows her to explore different musical styles and connect with diverse audiences. With her captivating performances and soulful renditions, she has garnered a dedicated fan base across various regions.

 

In addition to her singing career, Priya has also ventured into acting. Her talents extend beyond vocals, as she has demonstrated her acting skills in both films and television. Her on-screen presence and versatility as an actress have added depth to her artistic portfolio.

 

Priya's ability to sing and act in multiple languages highlights her versatility and adaptability as an artist. Her dedication to her craft and passion for music and acting shine through her performances, captivating audiences and leaving a lasting impact.

With her rising popularity and talent, Priya Patidar continues to make her mark in the entertainment industry. Her musical prowess and acting abilities, combined with her charisma and dedication, promise a bright future filled with exciting projects and memorable performances.

item.title: Priyadarshini
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Priyadarshini

Playback Female Singer

Priyadarshini Ram, also known as Priyadharshi Ram or simply Priyadarshini, is a Singaporean-Indian playback singer. She has made significant contributions to the Tamil, Kannada, Telugu, and Hindi film industries, having performed in over 180 movies. Additionally, she has sung more than 800 songs for devotional and private albums in 10 different languages.

 

Priyadarshini began her career as a playback singer with a duet song alongside Hariharan for the Tamil film "Kadhal Dot Com," which was released in 2004. She made her debut in Kannada films with the movie "Ajju," featuring music by Rajesh Ramanath, and also sang in Telugu cinema for D Imman. She has also lent her vocals to background vocals in the Hindi film "Garam Masala," starring Akshay Kumar. In 2008, she had a duet with S. P. Balasubrahmanyam in the Kannada movie "Rocky."

 

Throughout her career, Priyadarshini has collaborated with esteemed music directors such as Bharadwaj, D. Imman, Hamsalekha, Mano Murthy, Gurukiran, R. P. Patnaik, Rajesh Ramnath, K. Kalyan, S. A. Rajkumar, Mahesh Mahadev, M. N. Krupakar, Ravish, and others. She has also recorded jingles and albums.

 

In terms of education, Priyadarshini holds a Bachelor's degree in Electrical & Electronics Engineering from Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, a Master's degree in Music from the University of Madras, and a PhD in film music from the University of Mysore.

Priyanshi Srivastav

Playback Female Singer

Priyanshi Srivastav is a talented singer whose captivating voice and soulful renditions have earned her a special place in the hearts of music enthusiasts. With her remarkable vocal range and versatility, she has managed to leave a lasting impression in the music industry.

 

Priyanshi's journey as a singer began at a young age, displaying her innate talent and passion for music. Her dedication and hard work enabled her to hone her skills and become a rising star in the music scene. Whether it's classical melodies, peppy pop songs, or heart-wrenching ballads, Priyanshi effortlessly breathes life into every genre she touches.

 

Her performances are known for their emotional depth and the ability to evoke a wide range of emotions in her listeners. Priyanshi's melodious voice, coupled with her impeccable control and expression, creates a mesmerizing experience for her audience. Her performances are not just about singing, but about connecting with the hearts of her listeners.

 

Apart from her musical prowess, Priyanshi is also admired for her humble nature and down-to-earth personality. She exudes a certain warmth and authenticity that endears her to fans from all walks of life.

item.title: Ranina Reddy
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Ranina Reddy

Playback Female Singer

Ranina Reddy is an Indian playback singer known for her work in Tamil and Telugu cinema. She has collaborated with various music composers including Yuvan Shankar Raja, Harris Jayaraj, Devi Sri Prasad, Sai Thaman, Selva Ganesh, Raghu Dixit, and S.A. Rajkumar. Ranina Reddy made her presence felt in the Tamil film industry with her appearance in Venkat Prabhu's 2008 comedy thriller "Saroja." Since then, she has sung several songs, particularly for renowned composer Harris Jayaraj, establishing herself as a talented playback singer. Her soulful and versatile voice has graced numerous Tamil and Telugu film soundtracks, earning her recognition and praise. Ranina Reddy continues to contribute her melodic vocals to the South Indian film industry, collaborating with various music directors and leaving a mark with her performances.

item.content:encoded:
Rakshita Suresh

Playback Female Singer

Rakshita Suresh, born on June 1, 1998, is an Indian playback singer known for her work in Tamil, Hindi, Kannada, and Telugu cinema. She gained recognition through various music talent shows and has established herself as a versatile singer.

 

Rakshita's musical journey began at the age of 4 when she started learning music. She received training in Carnatic Music, Hindustani Classical music, and Light Music. Her talent and passion for singing led her to participate in several reality shows.

 

In Kannada, she appeared on shows like "Yede Thumbi Haduvenu" on ETV and "Junior Super Stars" on Star Vijay (Tamil). She emerged as the winner on "Rhythm Tadheem" aired on ETV Kannada and became the Title Winner of "Little Star Singer" in 2009, which was aired on Asianet Suvarna (Kannada). In 2018, she was the first runner-up on the reality show "Super Singer 6" aired on Star Vijay (Tamil), which garnered her significant attention.

 

Rakshita made her debut as a playback singer with renowned composer Ilayaraja. Since then, she has lent her voice to numerous songs in Tamil, Hindi, Kannada, and Telugu. Her Telugu debut song was recorded in 2015 for the film "Yevade Subramanyam" starring Nani. She has also performed solo concerts both in India and abroad, including the "Mysuru Yuva Dasara" event.

 

In Bollywood, Rakshita made her debut with the song "Yaane Yaane" composed by A.R. Rahman for the movie "Mimi."

item.title: Reena Bhardwaj
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Reena Bhardwaj

Playback Female Singer

Reena Bhardwaj is a British Indian singer, songwriter, and recording artist known for her versatile talent and collaborations with renowned musicians. Born and raised in London, Reena showed a strong inclination towards Indian arts, particularly music and dance, from a young age. She trained in the North Indian classical dance form Kathak and began performing on stage at the age of 9. As a teenager, her focus shifted to singing, and she captivated audiences with her effortless rendition of complex compositions.

 

While pursuing a professional career in Business Management and completing her Bachelor's and master's degrees from the London School of Economics, Reena continued to nurture her musical interests. It was during her master's degree that she received an unexpected call from her favorite Indian composer, A.R. Rahman, which marked a turning point in her musical career.

 

Reena's debut song, "Yeh Rishta," recorded with A.R. Rahman for the Bollywood film "Meenaxi: A Tale of Three Cities," propelled her to the top of the Indian music charts. She became the first British Asian artist to be nominated for a Zee Cine Award for Best Playback Singer and the MTV Immies Award for Best New Talent in 2004. She went on to collaborate with Rahman on various Bollywood and Tamil/Telugu film soundtracks, including "Mangal Pandey: The Rising," "Sakkarakatti," and "Raavan."

 

Another significant collaboration in Reena's career is with British Asian Composer/Producer Nitin Sawhney. She first gained recognition for her soulful rendition of the Indian poem "Heer" on Sawhney's album "Human" in 2003. She continued to work with Sawhney, co-writing songs and delivering memorable performances on his albums such as "Philtre" and "London Undersound." Reena has toured extensively with Sawhney and performed at prestigious venues like Glastonbury Festival, WOMAD, The Barbican Centre, and The Royal Albert Hall.

 

Reena Bhardwaj's talent extends beyond collaborations with Rahman and Sawhney. She has collaborated with Basement Jaxx, Trilok Gurtu, Talvin Singh, and Guy Chambers, showcasing her versatility in different genres and styles. Her songs have been featured on compilation CDs, including Ministry of Sound's "Angel Beach" and Sony Legacy's "The Best of AR Rahman."

item.title: Rekha Bhardwaj
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Rekha Bhardwaj

Playback Female Singer

Rekha Bhardwaj, born on 24 January 1964, is a renowned Indian singer and live performer. She has been honored with two Filmfare Awards and one National Award for her exceptional contributions to the music industry. While she primarily sings in Hindi, she has also showcased her talent in other languages such as Bengali, Marathi, Punjabi, and Malayalam.

 

Born in Delhi, Rekha Bhardwaj is one of six siblings, with five sisters and a brother. In 1991, she tied the knot with Vishal Bhardwaj, a prominent film director, composer, and playback singer. Their journey together began in 1984 when they first crossed paths while preparing for the annual function of Hindu College in New Delhi.

 

Rekha Bhardwaj's musical training started at home under the guidance of her older sister. Later, she received formal training from Pandit Amarnath, further honing her skills and enriching her musical prowess.

 

Her debut album, titled 'Ishqa Ishqa,' was released in 2002, a decade after its inception. The album's success brought her recognition and paved the way for career-defining songs such as "Namak Ishq Ka" in the 2006 film "Omkara," composed by her husband Vishal Bhardwaj. She also gained widespread acclaim for her rendition of "Sasural Genda Phool," a Chhattisgarhi folk song recreated by A.R. Rahman, in the 2009 film "Delhi-6."

 

Rekha Bhardwaj's soulful and versatile voice, coupled with her emotive performances, has made her a highly respected and sought-after singer in the Indian music industry. She continues to captivate audiences with her enchanting melodies and remains a prominent figure in the world of music.

item.title: Rimi Tomy
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Rimi Tomy

Playback Female Singer

Rimi Tomy is a multi-talented Indian artist known for her contributions as a playback singer, Carnatic musician, television host, and occasional actress. She began her career by hosting music programs on television and made her singing debut with the song "Chingamasam Vannu Chernnal" in the 2002 film "Meesa Madhavan," alongside co-singer Shanker Mahadevan.

 

In addition to her singing career, Rimi Tomy has anchored numerous television shows and has served as a judge on various reality shows spanning different genres. She has showcased her talent and versatility as a television host and entertainer.

 

Rimi Tomy ventured into acting with the Aashiq Abu film "5 Sundarikal," marking her debut as an actress. She later took on a lead role opposite Jayaram in the 2015 film "Thinkal Muthal Velli Vare." She has also made appearances in song sequences in films such as "Balram Vs Tharadas," "Kaaryasthan," and "916." Additionally, she has acted in various advertisements, showcasing her versatility across different mediums.

 

Born into a Syro-Malabar Catholic family in Pala, Kottayam, Rimi Tomy is the daughter of Tomy Joseph and Rani Tomy. She has a sister named Reenu Tomy and a brother named Rinku Tomy. Sadly, her father passed away on July 6, 2014, due to cardiac arrest.

 

Rimi Tomy's singing career took off when she joined the well-known troupe called Angel Voice. During a show with Angel Voice, she caught the attention of mimicry artist, composer, and lyricist Nadirshah. Impressed by her talent, he recommended her to Lal Jose, the director of the film "Meesa Madhavan," and film composer Vidyasagar. This breakthrough opportunity led to a successful singing career for Rimi Tomy.
