In addition to her singing career, Rimi Tomy has anchored numerous television shows and has served as a judge on various reality shows spanning different genres. She has showcased her talent and versatility as a television host and entertainer.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Rimi Tomy ventured into acting with the Aashiq Abu film \"5 Sundarikal,\" marking her debut as an actress. She later took on a lead role opposite Jayaram in the 2015 film \"Thinkal Muthal Velli Vare.\" She has also made appearances in song sequences in films such as \"Balram Vs Tharadas,\" \"Kaaryasthan,\" and \"916.\" Additionally, she has acted in various advertisements, showcasing her versatility across different mediums.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Born into a Syro-Malabar Catholic family in Pala, Kottayam, Rimi Tomy is the daughter of Tomy Joseph and Rani Tomy. She has a sister named Reenu Tomy and a brother named Rinku Tomy. Sadly, her father passed away on July 6, 2014, due to cardiac arrest.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Rimi Tomy's singing career took off when she joined the well-known troupe called Angel Voice. During a show with Angel Voice, she caught the attention of mimicry artist, composer, and lyricist Nadirshah. Impressed by her talent, he recommended her to Lal Jose, the director of the film \"Meesa Madhavan,\" and film composer Vidyasagar. This breakthrough opportunity led to a successful singing career for Rimi Tomy.<\/p>","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_weight":"bold"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":false}],"isInner":false},{"id":"5aaf9d6","elType":"section","settings":{"background_background":"classic","background_color":"#EAF0EE8F","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"ac4fb18"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"a1b2b38"}]},"elements":[{"id":"6427822","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":100,"_inline_size":null},"elements":[{"id":"7c19ec8","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Enquiry Form","header_size":"h3","align":"center","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_size":{"unit":"px","size":40,"sizes":[]},"typography_font_weight":"bold","_margin":{"unit":"px","top":"40","right":"0","bottom":"20","left":"0","isLinked":false},"__globals__":{"title_color":"globals\/colors?id=6d3d44f9"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"},{"id":"96f6011","elType":"widget","settings":{"shortcode":"[forminator_form id=\"5483\"]","_margin":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"40","left":"0","isLinked":false}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"shortcode"}],"isInner":false}],"isInner":false}]

item.title: Roopa Revathi
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Roopa Revathi

Playback Female Singer

Roopa Revathi, also known as Roopa K.R., is an Indian musician, violinist, and playback singer from Kerala. She began her career as a playback singer in the Malayalam movie "Madampi" in 2008 and has also recorded songs for Tamil and Kannada films. She gained recognition and popularity as the winner of the reality show "Amrita TV Super Star Global," a musical talent hunt show hosted by Amrita TV.

 

Roopa Revathi was born in Ernakulam, Kerala. She started learning Carnatic music at the age of five under the guidance of Malini Hariharan and Tamarakkadu Govindan Namboothiri. Currently, she continues her musical education under the guidance of P Unni Krishnan and M. Jayachandran.

 

In 2008, Roopa Revathi made her debut as a playback singer with the song "Ente Sharike" in B. Unnikrishnan's Malayalam film "Madampi," with music composed by M. Jayachandran. She showcased her talent and vocal abilities through this opportunity.

 

In 2011, Roopa Revathi also made her debut as a violinist in the Malayalam film industry with the film "Urumi," starring Prithviraj Sukumaran. The film had Deepak Dev as the composer.

 

Roopa Revathi has made significant contributions to the music industry, both as a playback singer and a violinist. Her talent and dedication have earned her recognition and a place among the notable musicians in the industry

item.title: Rupali Jagga
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Rupali Jagga

Playback Female Singer

Rupali Jagga is an exceptionally talented singer who has captivated audiences with her powerful and soulful voice. Hailing from India, she has carved a niche for herself in the music industry with her remarkable vocal range and versatility.

 

Rupali's journey in music began at a young age, and her passion for singing has only grown stronger over the years. Her ability to effortlessly blend different genres, including Bollywood, Sufi, and Western music, sets her apart as a unique artist. Whether she is belting out high-energy dance numbers or delivering heart-wrenching ballads, Rupali's performances are always filled with emotion and intensity.

 

Her exceptional talent has earned her recognition on various prestigious platforms. She has participated in popular reality singing competitions, where her electrifying stage presence and flawless vocals have garnered her widespread acclaim. Rupali's ability to connect with her audience on an emotional level is truly remarkable, leaving a lasting impression on everyone who hears her sing.

 

With her infectious energy, remarkable vocal prowess, and genuine passion for music, Rupali Jagga continues to make waves in the music industry. Her dedication and determination to constantly push boundaries and explore new musical territories make her a force to be reckoned with. As she continues to evolve as an artist, Rupali is bound to leave an indelible mark on the world of music.

Sanah Moidutty

Playback Female Singer

Sanah Moidutty is a talented singer known for her soulful and captivating voice. Hailing from Kerala, India, Sanah gained popularity through her YouTube channel, where she uploaded cover songs that showcased her exceptional vocal range and musicality. Her versatility shines through as she effortlessly navigates genres like Bollywood, Western pop, and regional music, leaving her listeners mesmerized.

 

Sanah's journey in the music industry has been remarkable. She has collaborated with renowned musicians and composers, lending her voice to several hit songs in the Indian film industry. Her ability to infuse emotions into her renditions has earned her a dedicated fan base worldwide.

 

Beyond her vocal prowess, Sanah's warm and genuine personality shines through her performances, connecting with her audience on a deeper level. She continues to explore her artistic boundaries, experimenting with new sounds and pushing herself to deliver extraordinary musical experiences.

 

With her unique blend of talent, passion, and dedication, Sanah Moidutty has carved a niche for herself in the music world and continues to inspire aspiring singers around the globe. Her star is undoubtedly on the rise, and her future in the industry looks promising and filled with more melodious treasures.

item.title: Sanchita Bhattacharya
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Sanchita Bhattacharya

Playback Female Singer

Sanchita Bhattacharya, born on 19 February 1992, is an accomplished Indian playback singer, composer, and television personality. She gained prominence at a young age when she participated in the singing competition show "Sa Re Ga Ma Pa L'il Champs." At the age of 14, she became the oldest winner in the history of the show and also the first female winner to be chosen by public voting. Her victory showcased her exceptional talent and garnered attention from the industry and music lovers alike.

 

Sanchita Bhattacharya has lent her melodious voice to numerous films and albums in various Indian languages. Her versatile singing skills have allowed her to explore and excel in different musical genres. As a playback singer and composer, she has contributed to the rich and diverse music scene in India.

 

Alongside her musical accomplishments, Sanchita Bhattacharya has also made a mark as a television personality. Her talent, dedication, and success have made her a respected figure in the Indian music industry.

item.title: Shakthisree Gopalan
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Shakthisree Gopalan

Playback Female Singer

Shakthisree Gopalan is an Indian vocalist, composer, songwriter, and performer known for her collaborations with top South Indian music composers like A.R. Rahman. She has made a name for herself in both film music and the independent music scene, exploring various genres such as Pop, R'n'B, trip-hop, and jazz.

 

Born and raised in Kochi, Kerala, Shakthisree completed her schooling at Rajagiri Public School, Kalamassery. She later moved to Chennai and pursued a degree in architecture at Anna University's School of Architecture and Planning. Alongside her studies, she received 13 years of training in Carnatic music.

 

In 2008, Shakthisree participated in the SS Music Voice Hunt and emerged as the winner of the second season. Although she was underage at the time, this experience paved the way for her entry into the film industry. She made her debut as a playback singer with the song "Taxi 4777."

 

In addition to her film career, Shakthisree has actively performed and released independent music in multiple languages. She has collaborated with the band "Off the Record," consisting of Vikram Vivekanand on guitar, Satish Narayanan on bass, and Tapas Naresh/Vinay Ramakrishnan on drums. She has showcased her talent at various cultural festivals, including those held at Madras Christian College, National Institute of Technology Tiruchirappalli, SASTRA University, VIT University, and Madras Institute of Technology.

item.title: Shalmali Kholgade
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Shalmali Kholgade

Playback Female Singer

Shalmali Kholgade is an Indian playback singer known for her work in Hindi language films. She has also sung in other Indian languages such as Marathi, Bengali, Telugu, and Tamil. Shalmali has received several awards, including a Filmfare Award and a Filmfare Award Marathi, and has been praised for her unique singing style.

 

Shalmali started performing at the age of 16 and received her music training from her mother, Uma Kholgade, an Indian classical singer and theatre personality. She furthered her music education under Shubhada Paradkar and was accepted by the Los Angeles College of Music, although she decided not to attend due to her recording commitments. Shalmali has showcased her versatility as a performer by participating in various musical projects. She has performed as a vocalist with Mikey McCleary's popular act 'The Bartender,' where she has given beautiful renditions of vintage Bollywood songs with a touch of sensuous, old school jazz. She has also performed as a soloist with a Latvian troupe in a Cabaret named Bombaloo, touring Moscow, Yerevan, and Armenia.

 

In 2012, Shalmali made her debut as a lead vocalist in Bollywood playback singing with the song "Pareshaan" from the film Ishaqzaade, composed by Amit Trivedi. The song became a critical and commercial success, topping charts across India. She won the Filmfare Award for Best Female Playback Singer for her performance in "Pareshaan." She continued to deliver hit songs, including "Daaru Desi" from Cocktail and "Aga Bai" from Aiyyaa in the same year.

 

In the following years, Shalmali achieved further success with songs like "Lat Lag Gayee" from Race 2, "Balam Pichkari" from Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani, and "Baby Ko Bass Pasand Hai" from Sultan. She has received critical acclaim for her singing style in various hit songs, such as "Aga Bai" from Aiyyaa, "Chingam Chabake" from Gori Tere Pyaar Mein, "Mohobbat Buri Bemari" from Bombay Velvet, "Shakira" from Welcome to Karachi, and "Naach Meri Jaan" from ABCD 2.

item.title: Shashaa Tirupati
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Shashaa Tirupati

Playback Female Singer

Shashaa Tirupati, born on December 21, 1989, is a Canadian playback singer, songwriter, and music producer of Indian descent. She is known for her versatile vocal skills and has recorded songs in over 20 languages, including Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Punjabi, Malayalam, Kannada, Bengali, Konkani, Arabic, and English. With more than 200 songs to her credit, she has established herself as a prominent figure in the Indian music industry.

 

Tirupati gained recognition as "The Humma Girl" for her rendition of the popular song "The Humma Song" from the film OK Jaanu. In 2018, she received the National Film Award for Best Female Playback Singer and the Filmfare Award for the Tamil song "Vaan Varuvaan" from the movie Kaatru Veliyidai.

 

Some of her notable Bollywood hits include "Khulke Jeene Ka" from Dil Bechara, "Phir Bhi Tumko Chahunga" (with Arijit Singh) and "Baarish" from Half Girlfriend, "Kanha" from Shubh Mangal Savdhan, and "O Sona Tere Liye" and "Chal Kahin Door" from the film Mom. She has also collaborated with renowned composer A.R. Rahman on several projects, including the films Dil Bechara and 99 Songs.

 

Apart from playback singing, Tirupati has ventured into independent music and released her first single, "In My Skin," from her debut EP titled "I'm Sorry, Heart" in January 2022. She is also involved in live performances and has toured extensively with A.R. Rahman, including concerts such as the Encore Tour, Infinite Love Tour, and Rahmanishq Tour.

 

In addition to her music career, Tirupati has showcased her acting skills in the theater. She made her theater acting debut in the play "I, Cloud," written and directed by Ulka Mayur, with lyricist Mayur Puri playing the male lead.

item.title: Shibani kashyap
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Shibani Kashyap

Playback Female Singer

Shibani Kashyap is an Indian singer known for her work in the Bollywood film industry. She gained fame for singing the signature tune of the AIR FM channel of All India Radio and Amul India. Kashyap specializes in a blend of Sufi and Western music.

 

Born in Delhi, India, Shibani Kashyap is a graduate in English literature from the University of Delhi. She has a background in both Western and Indian classical music. She was a member of the band Black Slade in Delhi before gaining national recognition for her debut pop album, "Ho Gayi Hai Mohabbat" in 1998, for which she won a Channel V award.

 

Kashyap has composed advertisement jingles for Amul India and the Subah Savere show on Doordarshan. She has performed live shows around the world and represented India at the annual international music festival Azia Dauysy held in Kazakhstan in 1999. She has also released a Sufi album called "Nagmagee" in 2000.

 

In addition to her singing career, Shibani Kashyap has ventured into acting. She made her acting debut in the Star Plus TV show "Veera" as the musician Megha. She has also acted in the film "Ranviir The Marshal" (2015) and sang a special number for it.

 

Kashyap has received accolades for her work, including winning the Best Female Pop Singer award for her album "Nazakat" at the 2005 Sangeet Awards in San Francisco.

Apart from her music career, Shibani Kashyap is known for her association with Buddhism, particularly Nichiren Buddhism. She believes in the power of inner change and has credited her faith with positively impacting her life.

 

In recent years, Kashyap has been involved in independent music projects and has been associated with platforms like ArtistAloud.com. She continues to contribute to the music industry and has released her own album titled "My Free Spirit."

In 2018, she collaborated with singer and composer Varun Ahuja on the gangster-themed song "Bachke tu chalna re" for the film "Mere Paas Baap Hai."

Shibani Kashyap is an Indian singer known for her work in the Bollywood film industry. She gained fame for singing the signature tune of the AIR FM channel of All India Radio and Amul India. Kashyap specializes in a blend of Sufi and Western music.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Born in Delhi, India, Shibani Kashyap is a graduate in English literature from the University of Delhi. She has a background in both Western and Indian classical music. She was a member of the band Black Slade in Delhi before gaining national recognition for her debut pop album, \"Ho Gayi Hai Mohabbat\" in 1998, for which she won a Channel V award.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Kashyap has composed advertisement jingles for Amul India and the Subah Savere show on Doordarshan. She has performed live shows around the world and represented India at the annual international music festival Azia Dauysy held in Kazakhstan in 1999. She has also released a Sufi album called \"Nagmagee\" in 2000.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

In addition to her singing career, Shibani Kashyap has ventured into acting. She made her acting debut in the Star Plus TV show \"Veera\" as the musician Megha. She has also acted in the film \"Ranviir The Marshal\" (2015) and sang a special number for it.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Kashyap has received accolades for her work, including winning the Best Female Pop Singer award for her album \"Nazakat\" at the 2005 Sangeet Awards in San Francisco.<\/p>

Apart from her music career, Shibani Kashyap is known for her association with Buddhism, particularly Nichiren Buddhism. She believes in the power of inner change and has credited her faith with positively impacting her life.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

In recent years, Kashyap has been involved in independent music projects and has been associated with platforms like ArtistAloud.com. She continues to contribute to the music industry and has released her own album titled \"My Free Spirit.\"<\/p>

In 2018, she collaborated with singer and composer Varun Ahuja on the gangster-themed song \"Bachke tu chalna re\" for the film \"Mere Paas Baap Hai.\"<\/p>","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_weight":"bold"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":false}],"isInner":false},{"id":"0b64d50","elType":"section","settings":{"background_background":"classic","background_color":"#EAF0EE8F","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"ac4fb18"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"a1b2b38"}]},"elements":[{"id":"679dff1","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":100,"_inline_size":null},"elements":[{"id":"4afac84","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Enquiry Form","header_size":"h3","align":"center","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_size":{"unit":"px","size":40,"sizes":[]},"typography_font_weight":"bold","_margin":{"unit":"px","top":"40","right":"0","bottom":"20","left":"0","isLinked":false},"__globals__":{"title_color":"globals\/colors?id=6d3d44f9"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"},{"id":"94a6217","elType":"widget","settings":{"shortcode":"[forminator_form id=\"5483\"]","_margin":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"40","left":"0","isLinked":false}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"shortcode"}],"isInner":false}],"isInner":false}]

item.title: Shilpa Rao
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Shilpa Rao

Playback Female Singer

Shilpa Rao, born Apeksha Rao on 11 April 1984, is an Indian singer hailing from Jamshedpur. She completed her Post Graduation in Applied Statistics from St. Xavier's College in Mumbai before venturing into her singing career. Rao initially worked as a jingle singer for three years before making her Bollywood debut in 2007 with the song "Tose Naina" from the film Anwar, which became a popular hit.

 

Her breakthrough came with the release of the songs "Woh Ajnabi" from The Train (2007) and "Khuda Jaane" from Bachna Ae Haseeno (2008), which earned her a nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Female Playback Singer. She further gained recognition for her collaboration with renowned composers like Ilaiyaraaja for Paa (2009) and A.R. Rahman for Jab Tak Hai Jaan (2012), Dhoom 3 (2013), and Bang Bang! (2014). Rao's association with Amit Trivedi resulted in notable songs such as "Manmarziyaan" from Lootera (2013).

 

Rao is known for her versatility and experimentation with different musical styles and genres. She was the final Indian singer to perform in Coke Studio Pakistan with the song "Paar Chanaa De" (2016). Additionally, her rendition of "Aaj Jaane Ki Zid Na Karo" from the deluxe edition of the Ae Dil Hai Mushkil soundtrack (2016) received critical acclaim.

 

Throughout her career, Rao has shown a willingness to explore new styles and collaborate with various composers and artists. She has been praised for her unique interpretations and expressions in her songs. In addition to her music career, Rao has also supported charitable organizations and causes.

item.title: Shirley Setia
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Shirley Setia

Playback Female Singer

Shirley Setia is a singer and actress originally from Daman, India, who gained fame through her work in the Indian film and music industries. Born in Daman, she immigrated with her family to Auckland, New Zealand. Setia rose to prominence as a YouTube musician, where she uploaded covers of Bollywood songs while studying at the University of Auckland. Her YouTube videos gained significant attention, leading to her being referred to as "Bollywood's Next Big Singing Sensation" by Forbes magazine.

 

Setia made her acting debut in the 2020 Hindi film "Maska," which was released on Netflix. She later appeared in the film "Nikamma" in 2022, marking her big-screen debut. She also starred in the Telugu film "Krishna Vrinda Vihari," which was released in September 2022.

 

In her singing career, Setia performed in concerts in Mumbai and Hyderabad in 2016 after gaining popularity on YouTube. She has amassed a significant following on her YouTube channel, with millions of subscribers and hundreds of millions of views. Setia has been recognized as India's YouTube sensation by the Hindustan Times and as one of New Zealand's biggest international artists by TVNZ.

 

Setia's journey from a YouTube musician to an actress has garnered attention and recognition, making her a rising star in the Indian entertainment industry.

item.title: Shreya Ghoshal
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Shreya Ghoshal

Playback Female Singer

Shreya Ghoshal is an Indian singer known for her wide vocal range and versatility. She is considered one of the most prolific and popular singers in India. Ghoshal has recorded songs for films and albums in various Indian languages and has received numerous accolades, including four National Film Awards, four Kerala State Film Awards, two Tamil Nadu State Film Awards, two BFJA Awards, seven Filmfare Awards, and ten Filmfare Awards South.

 

Ghoshal began learning music at the age of four and started her formal training in classical music at the age of six. She gained recognition at the age of sixteen when she won the television singing reality show "Sa Re Ga Ma." This led to her Bollywood playback singing debut in Sanjay Leela Bhansali's film "Devdas" (2002). Her song "Bairi Piya" from the film became an instant success, and she received a National Film Award for Best Female Playback Singer for her performance. Ghoshal also won a Filmfare Award for Best Female Playback Singer and the Filmfare RD Burman Award for New Music Talent.

 

In addition to her playback singing career, Ghoshal has appeared as a judge on several television reality shows and has been featured in music videos. She has received honors from the state of Ohio in the United States, where a day was declared as "Shreya Ghoshal Day," and she was honored in London by selected members of the House of Commons of the United Kingdom. Ghoshal has also been featured multiple times in Forbes' list of the top 100 celebrities from India. In 2017, she became the first Indian singer to have her wax figure displayed in the Indian wing of Madame Tussauds Museum in Delhi.

item.title: Shruti Pathak
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Shruti Pathak

Playback Female Singer

Shruti Pathak is an Indian playback singer and lyricist known for her work in the Hindi film industry. She was born and raised in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, and later moved to Mumbai to pursue a career in singing after completing her master's degree in Psychology. Pathak started her singing career by lending her voice to various remix albums. She gained popularity with her song "Mar Jawa" from the film Fashion (2008), for which she received nominations at the Filmfare Awards and Screen Awards. She also worked as a lyricist and singer for the song "Payaliya" from the film Dev.D (2009). She continued to showcase her talents as a singer and lyricist in films like Kai Po Che, where she wrote the song "Shubhaarambh" for Amit Trivedi. In addition to her film work, Shruti Pathak has performed in numerous stage shows and music festivals, including events at various universities and cultural fests. Shruti Pathak has been trained in classical music by her guru Shree Divyang Thakkar from a young age. item.title: Sithara
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Sithara Krishnakumar

Playback Female Singer

Sithara Krishnakumar is a versatile Indian artist who works as a playback singer, composer, lyricist, classical dancer, and occasional actor. While she predominantly works in Malayalam cinema, she has also contributed to Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada films. Sithara is known for her expertise in Hindustani and Carnatic classical music, as well as her skills as a ghazal singer.

 

She has received recognition and several awards for her talent, including three Kerala State Film Awards for Best Female Playback Singer. Sithara has traveled extensively, performing in concerts and stage shows worldwide. Apart from classical music, she also has a keen interest in folk and fusion genres. She has collaborated with popular musical bands in Kerala and has been part of international shows.

 

In 2014, Sithara formed a musical band called Eastraga, which focuses on female-oriented songs supported by a team of renowned musicians. She is also a member of the six-member band called Sithara's Project Malabaricus, which presents a contemporary blend of folk and classical songs.

 

Born into a family with a strong inclination towards classical arts, Sithara was introduced to music at a young age and started singing when she was just four years old. She received training in Carnatic music from Sri Ramanattukara Satheesan Master and Palai CK Ramachandran. She also received extensive education in Hindustani classical music from Ustad Fiyaz Khan. Additionally, she is a trained classical dancer under Kalamandalam Vinodini.

 

Sithara's career began as a dancer, and she later ventured into playback singing. Her debut as a playback singer came in 2007 with the song "Pammi Pammi" in the Malayalam film Athishayan. Before that, she had won several musical talent shows, including Asianet Saptha Swarangal, Kairali TV Gandharva Sangeetham, and Jeevan TV Voice.

She has collaborated with esteemed composers like Ouseppachan, M. Jayachandran, G. V. Prakash Kumar, Prashant Pillai, Gopi Sundar, Bijibal, and Shaan Rahman. Sithara has lent her voice to over 300 film songs in various languages.

item.title: Sivaangi Krishnakumar
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Sivaangi Krishnakumar

Playback Female Singer

Sivaangi Krishnakumar, popularly known as Sivaangi, is an Indian playback singer, actress, and television personality. She was born on May 25, 2000, in Trivandrum, Kerala, to a Malayali mother and Tamil father. Her father, Krishnakumar, is a singer and musicologist, while her mother, Binni Krishnakumar, is a playback singer. Both of her parents are recipients of the Kalaimamani Award. Sivaangi has a younger brother named Vinaayak Sunder.

Sivaangi completed her schooling at Chinmaya Vidyalaya in Virugambakkam, Chennai. She later pursued a bachelor's degree in Commerce at M.O.P. Vaishnav College for Women in Chennai. During her college days, she ventured into the music industry.

In 2019, Sivaangi gained recognition as a contestant on the Tamil reality television singing competition, Super Singer 7, which aired on Star Vijay. She showcased her singing talent on the show and received appreciation from the audience.

She then participated in the comedy cooking show, Cooku With Comali, which also aired on Star Vijay. Her performance on the show garnered her popularity and accolades. She received awards such as "The Entertaining Star Female" at the Blacksheep Digital Awards and "Most Popular Female in Reality Television" at the Behindwoods Gold Icons. She also won the "Trending Pair of the Year" award with Ashwin Kumar Lakshmikanthan at the Vijay Television Awards.

In 2020, Sivaangi made her acting debut in the comedy web series called Dear-u Brother-u, which garnered attention from the audience and netizens.

As a playback singer, Sivaangi made her debut in the Tamil film industry with the song "Anbaale Azhagaagum" from the movie Pasanga in 2009. She has since lent her voice to several songs in Tamil films, including "Talku Lessu Worku Moreu," "Machi," "Uruttu," "Nee En Usuru Pulla," "Sathiyama Sollurandi," "Bomma Bomma," "Neethanada," and "Rekkalu thodigi." She continues to work on new songs, with two set to be released in the second half of 2022.

Sivaangi has also ventured into acting, appearing in films such as Don, Naai Sekar Returns, and Kasethan Kadavulada.

item.title: Smita Bellur
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Smita Bellur

Playback Female Singer

Smita Bellur is a captivating Sufi singer whose soulful voice has captivated audiences around the world. Born and raised in India, Smita has dedicated her life to the pursuit of spiritual expression through music. With a unique blend of classical Indian and Sufi influences, her performances are a mesmerizing experience that transcends cultural boundaries.

 

Smita's voice has a divine quality, effortlessly weaving through intricate melodies and soaring to ethereal heights. Her renditions of ancient Sufi poetry evoke deep emotions, touching the hearts of listeners and transporting them to a realm of spiritual ecstasy. Whether performing in intimate gatherings or grand concert halls, Smita's presence on stage is magnetic, drawing the audience into a meditative state of bliss.

 

Beyond her musical prowess, Smita is a humble and deeply spiritual individual. She embraces the teachings of Sufism and incorporates them into her music, spreading messages of love, peace, and unity. Through her powerful performances and soul-stirring melodies, Smita Bellur continues to inspire and uplift the souls of all who have the privilege of experiencing her enchanting artistry.

item.title: Sona Mohapatra
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Sona Mohapatra

Playback Female Singer

Sona Mohapatra is an Indian singer, music composer, and lyricist. She was born on June 17, 1976. Sona holds a BTech degree in Mechanical Engineering from the College of Engineering and Technology, Bhubaneswar, and an MBA degree in Marketing & Systems from Symbiosis Centre for Management & HRD, Pune. Prior to her music career, she worked as a brand manager in Marico, handling brands like Parachute & Mediker.

 

Sona's journey in the music industry began with advertising jingles. She gained popularity for her jingle for Tata Salt - "Kal Ka Bharat Hai," and her song "Paas Aao Na" for Unilever's Close Up campaign, which was recorded in multiple languages and aired in 13 countries for four consecutive years. In 2007, she released her debut album "Sona" on Sony Records, which explored various musical styles such as rock, rhythm and blues, flamenco, Hindustani, Baul, and Romani music.

 

She has released several singles and songs for Bollywood films. Some of her notable works include the song "Bedardi Raja" from the movie "Delhi Belly" produced by Aamir Khan, the theme songs "Mujhe Kya Bechega Rupaiya" and "Ghar Yaad Aata Hai Mujhe" for the TV show "Satyamev Jayate," and the song "Jiya Laage Na" from the soundtrack of the film "Talaash." Sona is known for her electric live performances and has played at various venues, including the Lincoln Center in New York and stadium crowds in India.

Sona Mohapatra gained mainstream prominence through her appearances on the talk show "Satyamev Jayate" hosted by Aamir Khan. She frequently performed as a lead singer and was also the executive producer of the musical project associated with the show. Her cameo performances on the show garnered millions of views online. Sona is known for her efforts to promote women's empowerment and has contributed to projects that celebrate women's freedom.

Sona Mohapatra is married to Ram Sampath, a Bollywood song composer and music director. They met in 2002 and got married in 2005. Ram Sampath is known for his innovative music scores in films like "Delhi Belly," "Satyamev Jayate," and "Talaash." Sona and Ram are partners in their music production house called OmGrown Music and reside in Mumbai, where they have their own studios.

item.title: Sonu Kakkar
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Sonu Kakkar

Playback Female Singer

Sonu Kakkar is an Indian playback singer, songwriter, and television personality. She was born on October 20, 1979, in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand. Sonu Kakkar is known for her versatile singing style and has gained popularity for her contributions to the music industry.

 

Sonu Kakkar is the elder sister of popular Bollywood singers Neha Kakkar and Tony Kakkar. She has established herself as a talented playback singer and has lent her voice to numerous Hindi film songs. One of her most famous performances was in the song "Madari" which she performed with Vishal Dadlani in Coke Studio. The song was composed by Clinton Cerejo and received widespread acclaim.

 

In addition to playback singing, Sonu Kakkar has also released independent singles and collaborated with other artists. Her recent song "Sun Baliye" features Gajendra Verma and herself as the vocalists. The music video of the song includes Gajendra Verma and Apoorva Arora.

 

Sonu Kakkar continues to actively contribute to the music industry with her soulful voice and versatile singing skills.

item.title: Sravana Bhargavi
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Sravana Bhargavi

Playback Female Singer

Ravuri Sravana Bhargavi is an Indian playback singer known for her work in the Telugu music industry. She was born on 16 August 1989. Sravana Bhargavi has recorded several songs in Telugu films, showcasing her vocal talent.

She holds a B.Tech. degree from Vignan Institute of Technology and Science in Hyderabad and is currently pursuing an M.B.A. degree.

Sravana Bhargavi got engaged to singer Vedala Hemachandra on 9 December 2012 in Hyderabad, India, and they got married on 14 February 2013. They have a daughter named Shikhara Chandrika, who was born on 2 July 2016.

Apart from her singing career, Bhargavi has also ventured into other areas of the entertainment industry. She hosted a show on 92.7 Big FM in Hyderabad and has done voice acting in films like Love Failure and Gabbar Singh.

Additionally, she has co-hosted the television show "Bol Baby Bol" alongside her husband Hemachandra, which airs on Gemini TV. She has also participated in the TV show "Super Singer," which was telecasted on MAA TV. Sravana Bhargavi's versatility and talent have allowed her to make a mark in both singing and hosting in the Telugu entertainment industry.

Playback Female Singer

Srushti's musical journey began at a young age, and she honed her skills through rigorous training and constant practice. Her dedication and commitment to her craft have earned her recognition and admiration from both fans and industry professionals.

 

Not only does Srushti possess a remarkable voice, but she also possesses a magnetic stage presence that captivates audiences. Her performances are a perfect blend of passion, emotion, and impeccable vocal control, leaving listeners spellbound.

 

As she continues to evolve as an artist, Srushti Tawde's star power only continues to rise. With her extraordinary talent and unwavering passion for music, she is poised to become a prominent figure in the music industry, enchanting audiences around the world with her soulful voice and artistic brilliance.

item.title: Sunanda Sharma
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Sunanda Sharma

Playback Female Singer

Sunanda Sharma is an Indian playback singer and film actress. She was born on 30 January 1992. Sharma gained recognition with her debut song "Billi Akh." She then ventured into acting, making her debut in the film Sajjan Singh Rangroot, alongside Diljit Dosanjh and Yograj Singh. She also made her entry into Bollywood with the song "Tere Naal Nachna."

Sunanda Sharma initially gained popularity by singing cover songs and sharing video recordings on YouTube. Her talent and growing fan base led her to release her debut single, "Billi Akh." One of her most popular songs, "Jaani Tera Naa," released in 2017, has amassed over 334 million views on YouTube.

She has received several accolades for her work in the music industry. She won the Best Debut Female Vocalist award at the PTC Punjabi Music Awards. In 2017, she was honored with the Best Female Act award at the Brit Asia TV Music Awards. Sharma's song "Baarish Ki Jaaye" has been well-received by audiences across India.

In addition to her singing and acting career, Sunanda Sharma has also worked as an anchor, hosting the show "Hunar Punjab Da - Season 2," which was telecasted on PTC Punjabi Channel. She has earned the reputation of being the New Boss Lady of the Music Industry in India.

item.title: Sunidhi Chauhan
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Sunidhi Chauhan

Playback Female Singer

Sunidhi Chauhan is an Indian playback singer known for her versatility. She was born on 14 August 1983 in Delhi, India. Chauhan began performing at a young age and made her career debut at the age of 13 in the film Shastra (1996). She gained recognition after winning the singing reality show Meri Awaz Suno and recorded the song "Ruki Ruki Si Zindagi" from Mast (1999), which won her the Filmfare RD Burman Award for New Music Talent.

 

Chauhan had several breakthrough moments in her career. In 2000, she received a Filmfare nomination for the song "Mehboob Mere" from Fiza. Her song "Dhoom Machale" from Dhoom (2004) earned her another Filmfare nomination. She received further nominations for songs like "Kaisi Paheli" and "Deedar De" from Parineeta and Dus (both in 2005). In 2006, she won her first Filmfare award for the song "Beedi" from Omkara and received two more nominations.

 

Chauhan continued to deliver popular songs, including the title track of Aaja Nachle (2007) and "Sajnaaji Vaari." She received her twelfth Filmfare nomination for the song "Chor Bazaari" from Love Aaj Kal (2009) and won her second Filmfare award for the item song "Sheila Ki Jawani" (2010). She also made her international singing debut with an alternate version of Enrique Iglesias' song "Heartbeat."

item.title: Sunitha Sarathy
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Sunitha Sarathy

Playback Female Singer

Sunitha Sarathy is an Indian vocalist and performer known for her work in both Indian contemporary and Western classical music genres. She is also a gospel singer and has performed in various church choirs. Sarathy gained recognition after winning the "Virgin Voice Choice" contest in 2000, a joint initiative of Channel V and Virgin Records. This paved the way for her debut in film playback singing in 2002.

She made her playback singing debut in the Tamil film "Yei! Nee Romba Azhagey Irruke," where she sang the prelude and interlude portions of the song "Ini Naanum Naanillai" along with Srinivas and Sujatha Mohan as the lead singers. Sarathy has lent her voice to around 200 film songs in various languages and has showcased her versatility as a singer-keyboardist-percussionist across different Western music genres such as classical, jazz, soul and R&B, neo-soul, and quiet storm. She has also recorded numerous gospel songs.

Coming from a family with a background in Western music, Sarathy began singing in choirs from a young age. Her mother, Susheela Sarathy, is a pianist and conductor of leading Madras choirs. Sarathy's talent was evident early on, and she gained recognition within Madras' church music circles for her performances, including devotionals in Latin and renditions of Franz Schubert's "Ave Maria." She has had the honor of rendering the 'Easter Proclamation' at San Thome Basilica.

After winning the Virgin Voice Choice contest, Sarathy caught the attention of playback singer Srinivas, who offered her a small portion of a song in the film "Hey! Nee Romba Azhaga Irukke" in 2002. She later received a big break and wider recognition with the full-length solo song "Thoodu Varuma" in the Tamil blockbuster film "Kaakha Kaakha." Sarathy gained national recognition for her playback singing in the Hindi-Tamil bilingual film "Yuva/Aaytha Ezhuthu" in 2004, directed by Mani Ratnam and composed by A. R. Rahman.

Since then, Sarathy has recorded her voice for several successful soundtracks in various languages, including films like "Mitr, My Friend," "Anniyan," "Polladhavan," "Vallavan," "Kana Kandaen," "Don 2," "Happy Days," "Sainikudu," and "Cheluvina Chittara." She has also ventured into international collaborations, recording the song "Warriors in Peace" for the Mandarin film "Warriors of Heaven and Earth" composed by A. R. Rahman. Sarathy has performed at various events, including the 2006 Asian Games.

item.title: Tia Bajpai
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Tia Bajpai

Playback Female Singer

Tia Bajpai is an Indian actress and singer who primarily works in the Hindi film industry. She was born on February 22, 1987, in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India.

 

Tia Bajpai made her acting debut with the film "Haunted - 3D" in 2011, directed by Vikram Bhatt. Her performance in the film received positive reviews, and she was nominated for several awards for her portrayal of the character Meera Sabharwal. She also lent her voice to some of the film's songs, showcasing her singing talent.

 

Following her debut, Tia Bajpai appeared in films like "Lanka," "1920: Evil Returns," and "Desi Kattey." She has acted in a variety of genres, including horror, thriller, and drama. Tia has also made appearances in web series and short films.

 

In addition to acting, Tia Bajpai is a trained classical singer and has released several music singles. She has showcased her vocal abilities in films and independent music projects.

Tia Bajpai continues to pursue her acting and singing career, and she is known for her versatility and dedication to her craft.

item.title: Tia Kar
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Tia Kar

Playback Female Singer

Tia Kar is a remarkable contestant who emerged as a shining star on the fifth season of Indian Idol. Hailing from a small town, her journey to the stage of this prestigious singing competition was nothing short of extraordinary. Tia possesses an innate talent that captivates audiences with her melodious voice and impeccable vocal range.

 

From the moment she stepped on the Indian Idol stage, Tia's performances were a testament to her versatility as a singer. Whether it was delivering soulful renditions of classic Bollywood numbers or infusing contemporary hits with her unique style, she always left the judges and viewers spellbound.

 

What sets Tia apart is not just her technical prowess, but also her ability to connect with the emotions of a song. Her heartfelt expressions and genuine passion have the power to touch hearts and evoke a myriad of emotions among listeners. Tia's stage presence is electrifying, commanding attention and leaving an indelible impression.

 

Throughout the competition, Tia has consistently displayed her dedication, hard work, and a hunger for perfection. Her humility and down-to-earth nature have won the hearts of millions, making her a beloved contestant.

item.title: Vaishali made
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Vaishali Mhade

Playback Female Singer

Vaishali Mhade is an Indian singer known for her participation and victory in Zee TV's reality series, Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Challenge 2009. She was born on August 21, 1984, in Hinganghat, Vidarbha, Maharashtra, India. Vaishali primarily sings in the Marathi language.

 

In Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Challenge 2009, Vaishali Mhade reached the top 3 along with Soumen Nandi and Yashita Yashpal Sharma. Due to her substantial fan following across India, she emerged as the winner of the competition. As a result, she received a Rs 50-lakh music contract with Zee TV, a Hyundai i10 car, and an LCD TV. Throughout the show, she showcased her versatility and consistency as a singer. She was a part of Himesh Reshammiya's "Rock Gharana." Prior to this, she had also won the Marathi version of Sa Re Ga Ma Pa in 2008.

 

Apart from her success in reality shows, Vaishali Mhade has pursued a career in the music industry. She has sung the title track for the Marathi daily soap "Kulvadhu" on Zee Marathi. Additionally, she lent her vocals to Shridhar Phadke's album "Sangeet Manmohee Re." She was a special invitee at the 2009 Nagpur International Marathon, where she shared the stage with Olympic gold medalist Abhinav Bindra.

 

In Bollywood, Vaishali made her singing debut with the song "Hum Tum" in the movie "Damadamm!" (2011), which was a duet with Himesh Reshammiya. She has also performed on the live TV show "Lord Buddha." Notably, she provided playback vocals for the popular duet song "Pinga" along with Shreya Ghoshal in the movie "Bajirao Mastani" (2015), which features Deepika Padukone and Priyanka Chopra. She also sang "Fitoori" in the same film. Vaishali has also sung the title tracks for Marathi TV shows like "Honar Sun Me Ya Gharchi" and "Mazya Navryachi Baayko." She recently collaborated with Shreya Ghoshal for the song "Ghar More Pardesiya" in the movie "Kalank."

item.title: Tulsi Kumar
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Tulsi Kumar

Playback Female Singer

Tulsi Kumar Dua, known as Tulsi Kumar, is an Indian playback singer, radio jockey, musician, and actress in the Bollywood industry. She was born to Gulshan Kumar, a renowned singer and the owner of T-Series, and Sudesh Kumari. Tulsi Kumar is the sister of film producer Bhushan Kumar and actress Khushali Kumar.

 

In addition to her work in the Bollywood industry, Tulsi Kumar owns Kids Hut, a YouTube channel under the T-Series label that features children's content such as nursery rhymes and stories.

Tulsi Kumar released her debut album, "Love ho Jaaye," in 2009, which included a music video for the title track. She gained recognition for her songs "Mujhe Teri" from the movie Paathshaala and "Tum Jo Aaye" from Once Upon a Time in Mumbaai.

 

Throughout her career, Tulsi Kumar has sung popular tracks such as "Mainu Ishq Da Lagya Rog," which featured her sister Khushali in her screen debut. She has also collaborated with other artists on songs like "Soch Na Sake," "Sanam Re," "Nachange Sari Raat," "Ishq Di Latt," "Salamat," "Dekh Lena," "Wajah Tum Ho," "Dil Ke Pass," "Dil Mein Chupa Lunga," and "Enni Soni" with Guru Randhawa.

 

During the COVID-19 lockdown in 2020, Tulsi Kumar released several songs, including collaborations with Darshan Raval on "Tere Naal" and Millind Gaba on "Naam." Her single "Tanhaai" became a blockbuster hit, amassing over 110 million views on YouTube.

 

In 2021, Tulsi Kumar released the single "Pehle Pyaar Ka Pehla Gham" with Jubin Nautiyal, featuring her sister Khushali and Parth Samthaan in the music video. She also released "Main Jis Din Bhula Doon" with Nautiyal, featuring Himansh Kohli and Sneha Namanandi.

Tulsi Kumar has received several accolades for her work, including the International Indian Film Academy (IIFA) award for Best Female Playback Singer in 2017 for the song "Soch Na Sake" and the Mirchi Music Award for Listener's Choice Song of the Year in 2017 for the same song. She has also been nominated for the IIFA Best Female Playback Singer in 2010 and 2019. The soundtrack to the film Kabir Singh, for which she provided vocals, won the Mirchi Music Award for Best Album in 2020.

item.title: Ujjaini Mukherjee
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Ujjaini Mukherjee

Playback Female Singer

Ujjaini Mukherjee is a talented singer who has made a significant mark in the music industry with her mesmerizing voice and versatile singing style. Born and raised in Kolkata, India, Ujjaini began her musical journey at a young age and soon emerged as a prominent figure in the world of Indian playback singing.

 

With her soulful renditions and impeccable vocal range, Ujjaini has won the hearts of millions of music lovers across the globe. Her ability to effortlessly transition between different genres, including classical, folk, and contemporary, showcases her versatility as an artist. Ujjaini's voice carries a unique blend of power, grace, and emotive depth, making her performances truly captivating.

 

Ujjaini has lent her voice to numerous hit songs in the Indian film industry and has collaborated with renowned composers and musicians. Her contributions to the music industry have been recognized with several awards and accolades, cementing her position as one of the most sought-after singers in the country.

 

Beyond her musical achievements, Ujjaini is also known for her humility, dedication, and passion for her craft, making her an inspiration to aspiring singers. With her talent and determination, Ujjaini Mukherjee continues to leave an indelible mark on the world of music.

item.title: Vaishali Samant
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Vaishali Samant

Playback Female Singer

Vaishali Samant is an Indian music composer, lyricist, and playback singer known for her work in the Marathi film and music industry. She has also sung in various other languages including Bengali, Gujarati, Bhojpuri, Assamese, Tamil, and Telugu. With a career spanning several years, she has sung over 2000 songs in Marathi.

Vaishali Samant has collaborated with renowned music composers such as A. R. Rahman in films like Lagaan, Taal, and Saathiya. She has also lent her voice to Bollywood films including Padmashree Laloo Prasad Yadav, Girlfriend, Eight, Malamaal Weekly, Tujhe Meri Kasam, Chetna, Dil Jo Bhi Kahe, Traffic Signal, Chamku, and Mirch. One of her most popular songs is "Chalka Re" from the movie Saathiya composed by A. R. Rahman.

In addition to her film work, Vaishali Samant has appeared as a judge on various reality singing competition shows. Her talent and contributions to the music industry have been recognized through nominations and awards. She was nominated for the Favorite Artist, India category at the MTV Asia Music Awards in 2004. In 2017, she received a nomination for Best Singer (Female) for her song "Gadbad Gondhal" at the Ambarnath Marathi Film Festival.

Vaishali Samant's versatility as a singer and her dedication to her craft have made her a prominent figure in the Marathi music industry. She continues to contribute her talent and passion to the field, delighting audiences with her melodious voice.

item.title: Vandana Srinivasan
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Vandana Srinivasan

Playback Female Singer

Vandana Srinivasan is an Indian playback singer known for her work in the South Indian film industry, particularly in Kollywood (Tamil cinema). She has also established herself as an independent singer.

 

Vandana's musical journey began at a young age when she started training in Carnatic Classical music under her guru, Mrs. Seetha Krishnan. She continued her musical education in Hindustani Classical music under the guidance of her guru, Mrs. Tanushree Saha, while pursuing a degree in Psychology at Women's Christian College (University of Madras) in Chennai. Later, she moved to London to pursue a postgraduate degree in Organizational & Social Psychology from the London School of Economics & Political Science.

 

During her time in London, Vandana was exposed to various musical influences and developed an interest in exploring Bangla music. After returning to Chennai in 2011, she established herself as an independent musician and playback singer in the film industry. Her versatile singing style and ability to adapt to different genres have garnered her recognition and opportunities in the industry.

 

In 2017, Vandana gave a TEDx talk on the life of a musician, sharing her experiences and insights. She is also actively involved in collaborations through her initiative called Musicalorie Productions, where she works with different artists on creative projects.

 

Outside of her musical career, Vandana is married to Anand Pattathil, a businessman, and they are settled in Chennai. Together, they run an online boutique called anastoriesonline, which showcases their creative endeavors.

item.title: Yashita Sharma
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Yashita Sharma

Playback Female Singer

Yashita Sharma is an Indian playback singer known for her work in the Bollywood music industry. She was born on January 27, 1986, in New Delhi, India.

 

Yashita gained recognition after participating in the reality singing competition "India's Raw Star" in 2014. She was mentored by singer and composer Himesh Reshammiya during the show. Her powerful and versatile voice impressed the judges and audience alike, leading to her success on the show.

 

Since then, Yashita Sharma has lent her voice to various Bollywood films and songs. Some of her notable tracks include "Gallan Goodiyaan" from the movie "Dil Dhadakne Do" (2015), "Chaandaniya" from "2 States" (2014), and "Radha" from "Student of the Year" (2012). Her energetic and soulful renditions have garnered her appreciation from music lovers.

 

Yashita Sharma continues to actively contribute to the music industry, collaborating with renowned composers and singers. Her dynamic vocal range and versatility have established her as a talented playback singer in Bollywood.

item.title: Yohani De Silva
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Yohani De Silva

Playback Female Singer

Yohani Diloka de Silva, born on July 30, 1993, is a multi-talented artist from Sri Lanka. She is known as a singer-songwriter, rapper, record producer, and YouTuber. Yohani initially started her music career as a YouTuber, gaining recognition for her rap cover of the song "Deviyange Bare." Her covers of various songs, showcasing her singing and rapping skills, earned her the title of "Rap Princess" in Sri Lanka. However, she gained significant global recognition and rose to prominence with her cover of the hit song "Manike Mage Hithe."

Yohani holds the distinction of being the first Sri Lankan female singer to amass over 3.60 million subscribers on YouTube. Her talent and popularity have garnered her a strong following, both in Sri Lanka and internationally.

Born in Colombo, Sri Lanka, Yohani is the daughter of Major General Prasanna de Silva, a former Army officer, and Dinithi de Silva, a former cabin crew member at Sri Lankan Airlines. She follows the Buddhist faith and has been practicing Buddhism since her early life. Yohani has a younger sister named Shavindri de Silva, who is currently pursuing a medical degree. Growing up, Yohani and her sister experienced life in various Army bases due to their father's military background.

Yohani's passion for music was nurtured from a young age, with her mother recognizing her talent and encouraging her to pursue it further. She was exposed to a variety of musical genres, as her parents listened to artists such as Bee Gees, Spice Girls, AR Rahman, and Elton John. Yohani completed her higher education in Logistics Management and Professional Accounting from the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University before embarking on her music career. She also obtained a master's degree in accounting from CQUniversity Australia.

In March 2019, Yohani returned to Sri Lanka, marking a significant turning point in her music career. She joined Pettah Effect, a record label co-founded by Dilanjan, where she had the opportunity to work alongside young talent. Yohani's talent and popularity led to several opportunities, including being appointed as the Brand Ambassador for Prima Kottu Mee, a notable endorsement for her as an artist. In August 2020, Yohani signed with Red Bull Records, and her debut single "Aaye" premiered under the label. She continued to release new music, including collaborations such as "Sitha Dawuna" with Chamath Sangeeth in September 2020.

item.title: Ajay-Atul
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Ajay-Atul

Music Composer

Ajay and Atul Gogavale, the acclaimed music composer duo and brothers, have made a significant impact in both the Marathi and Hindi film industries. Their unique blend of traditional and unconventional music styles has garnered them widespread recognition. They have a deep-rooted connection to their cultural heritage, extensive musical knowledge, and a strong commitment to working with live orchestras, which sets them apart in an era dominated by electronic music. With their exceptional talent and passion for acoustic sound, Ajay and Atul have breathed new life into Indian music. They have composed chart-topping songs for several successful films, including Agneepath, Sairat, and Jogwa. Their compositions have earned them over 65 accolades for music direction, including the prestigious National Film Awards. Their consistent success has also earned them a spot on the Forbes India Celebrity 100 list. The duo's musical prowess extends beyond films. They have composed music for albums, television serials, and stage plays, showcasing their versatility and range. Their notable works can be seen in movies such as Savarkhed: Ek Gaon, Natarang, PK, Singham, Dhadak, Tumbbad, Mauli, Zero, Manasu Malligey, Super 30, Panipat, and Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior. Each composition reflects their creativity, attention to detail, and ability to evoke emotions through music. Ajay and Atul's compositions have resonated with audiences and have become an integral part of the films they are associated with. They have successfully blended traditional elements with contemporary styles, creating a distinct musical identity. Their use of live orchestras adds depth and richness to their compositions, enhancing the overall cinematic experience. With their immense contributions to the world of music, Ajay and Atul Gogavale have firmly established themselves as one of the leading composer duos in India. Their ability to infuse soul and passion into their compositions has garnered them a dedicated fan base and critical acclaim. Their work continues to shape the landscape of Indian music, leaving an indelible mark on the industry.

item.title: D. Imman
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
D. Imman

Playback Female Singer

D. Imman is a renowned Indian music composer, known for his exceptional work in the Tamil and Telugu film industries. Born on January 24, 1983, in Chennai, he developed a deep passion for music at a young age and began his musical journey as a keyboard player. With his immense talent and dedication, Imman soon ventured into composing music for films. Imman made his debut as a music director in the Tamil film industry with the movie "Thamizhan" in 2002. Since then, there has been no looking back for him. He has composed music for numerous successful films, consistently delivering hit songs that have captivated audiences across the country. Imman's compositions are known for their versatility, as he seamlessly blends various genres, including folk, classical, and contemporary, to create soul-stirring melodies. One of the defining aspects of Imman's music is his ability to evoke emotions through his compositions. Whether it is a peppy dance number or a soulful ballad, his music has the power to connect with listeners on a deep level. Imman's ability to understand the pulse of the audience and his skill in crafting melodies that resonate with them have made him a highly sought-after music composer in the industry. Apart from his skillful compositions, Imman is also known for his collaborative spirit. He has worked with some of the most prominent filmmakers and actors in the industry, creating memorable musical scores that enhance the overall cinematic experience. His ability to work with different directors and adapt to their unique visions has earned him immense respect and admiration. Overall, D. Imman's contribution to the music industry is unparalleled. His passion for music, versatility, and ability to connect with the audience through his compositions have made him one of the most celebrated music composers in the Tamil and Telugu film industries. Imman's talent and dedication continue to leave a lasting impact on the world of music, and his melodious tunes will be cherished for years to come.

item.title: Deepak Dev
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Deepak Dev

Music Composer

Deepak Dev is a prominent Indian music composer known for his exceptional talent and versatility in the film industry. With his melodious compositions and remarkable understanding of various genres, he has established himself as a force to be reckoned with in the world of music. Deepak Dev started his journey as a composer in the early 2000s and quickly gained recognition for his exceptional work. He made his mark with his debut film, "Chronic Bachelor," which received critical acclaim for its soulful and catchy songs. Since then, there has been no looking back for Deepak Dev, as he continued to deliver one hit after another. One of the reasons for Deepak Dev's success is his ability to adapt to different musical styles and genres. Whether it is a romantic ballad, peppy dance number, or a haunting background score, he effortlessly captures the essence of the story through his compositions. His ability to create music that complements the visuals and enhances the emotional impact of the scenes is truly commendable. Deepak Dev has worked with some of the biggest names in the Indian film industry and has been a part of numerous blockbuster films. His work in movies like "Urumi," "D Company," and "Casanova" has been widely appreciated for its innovation and brilliance. Apart from his work in films, Deepak Dev has also been involved in various independent music projects and live concerts. He has showcased his exceptional talent on stage, mesmerizing audiences with his soul-stirring compositions.

item.title: G.V. Prakash Kumar
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
G.V. Prakash Kumar

Music Composer

G.V. Prakash Kumar, born on June 13, 1987, is a highly talented Indian music composer, singer, and actor. He comes from a family deeply rooted in the film industry, with his father being the renowned composer and conductor, G. Venkatesh. From a young age, Prakash Kumar displayed an innate musical talent and began learning the keyboard at the age of six. G.V. Prakash Kumar made his debut as a music composer in 2006 with the Tamil film "Veyil," which garnered critical acclaim and brought him recognition in the industry. Since then, he has composed music for numerous successful films across different languages, including Tamil, Telugu, and Hindi. His compositions have a unique and refreshing blend of traditional and contemporary sounds, making him a sought-after composer among filmmakers. What sets G.V. Prakash Kumar apart is his versatility and ability to create music that perfectly suits the mood and theme of a film. Whether it's a peppy and foot-tapping number or a soulful and emotional melody, he has a knack for creating music that resonates with the audience. Some of his notable compositions include "Aaromale" from the film "Vinnaithaandi Varuvaayaa," "Otha Sollaala" from "Aadukalam," and "Kannala Kannala" from "Thani Oruvan." Apart from his exceptional talent as a music composer, G.V. Prakash Kumar has also showcased his skills as a playback singer. His melodious voice has lent itself to several hit songs, adding an extra dimension to his musical endeavors. Furthermore, he has ventured into acting and has made a successful transition to the silver screen with notable performances in films like "Darling" and "Naachiyaar."

item.title: Ghibran
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Ghibran

Music Composer

Ghibran is a highly talented and accomplished music composer known for his exceptional work in the Indian film industry. With his unique style and innovative approach to music composition, he has carved a niche for himself in the industry. Ghibran's compositions are characterized by their melodious tunes, captivating arrangements, and experimental soundscapes.

 

One of the remarkable aspects of Ghibran's music is his ability to seamlessly blend various genres and experiment with different musical elements. Whether it's incorporating classical Indian instruments like the sitar and tabla or infusing electronic beats, he constantly pushes the boundaries of traditional film music. This versatility has earned him immense respect from both critics and audiences.

 

Ghibran has worked on a diverse range of films across multiple languages, including Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Hindi. His collaborations with renowned directors have resulted in numerous successful soundtracks, which have garnered critical acclaim and widespread popularity. Some of his notable works include "Vaagai Sooda Vaa," "Vikram Vedha," "Ratsasan," and "Kaithi."

 

Apart from his film compositions, Ghibran has also composed music for various stage productions and independent albums. His passion for music and his constant drive to create something new and refreshing have made him a sought-after composer in the industry.

 

Ghibran's dedication to his craft and his meticulous attention to detail have made him a favorite among filmmakers and actors. His ability to capture the emotions and essence of a story through his music is truly commendable. With each project, he brings a distinct flavor to the table, enhancing the overall cinematic experience.

In conclusion, Ghibran's talent and creativity as a music composer have made him a force to be reckoned with in the Indian film industry. His ability to create mesmerizing compositions that transcend genres and boundaries is a testament to his remarkable skill and passion for music. Ghibran's contributions to the world of film music have undoubtedly left an indelible mark, and he continues to inspire and captivate audiences with his extraordinary compositions.

item.title: Gopi Sundar
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Gopi Sundar

Music Composer

Gopi Sundar is a highly acclaimed music composer and playback singer in the Indian film industry. Born on May 30, 1977, in Kochi, Kerala, Gopi Sundar, whose real name is Gopinathan Velayudhan Nair, has created a significant impact with his soulful and melodious compositions.

With an exceptional ability to fuse different genres and styles, Gopi Sundar has managed to carve a niche for himself in the world of film music. His compositions are known for their versatility, innovative arrangements, and captivating melodies. He has the uncanny ability to tailor his music to perfectly fit the mood and narrative of the movies he works on, enhancing the overall cinematic experience.

 

Gopi Sundar's journey in the music industry began as a keyboard player in the popular band "Gopi Sundar & Team" before he ventured into film music composition. He gained recognition with his debut composition for the Malayalam film "Notebook" in 2006. Since then, he has worked on numerous successful projects in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, and Hindi cinema.

 

Some of his notable works include the soundtracks for films like "Bangalore Days," "Charlie," "Premam," and "Geetha Govindam." His compositions have won several prestigious awards, including Filmfare and Kerala State Film Awards.

 

Apart from his exceptional composition skills, Gopi Sundar is also a talented playback singer. He has lent his melodious voice to some of his own compositions and has also collaborated with other renowned playback singers.

With an exceptional ability to fuse different genres and styles, Gopi Sundar has managed to carve a niche for himself in the world of film music. He has the uncanny ability to tailor his music to perfectly fit the mood and narrative of the movies he works on, enhancing the overall cinematic experience.<\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Gopi Sundar's journey in the music industry began as a keyboard player in the popular band \"Gopi Sundar & Team\" before he ventured into film music composition. Since then, he has worked on numerous successful projects in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, and Hindi cinema.<\/p>

item.title: Harris Jayaraj
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Harris Jayaraj

Music Composer

Harris Jayaraj is a highly acclaimed and popular music composer in the Indian film industry. Born on January 8, 1975, in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, he has made a significant impact with his melodious and catchy tunes. With a career spanning over two decades, Harris Jayaraj has composed music for numerous blockbuster films, earning him a loyal fan base and critical acclaim.

 

Harris Jayaraj's music is known for its unique blend of western and Indian classical elements, resulting in a refreshing and contemporary sound. He has a remarkable ability to create soul-stirring melodies that resonate with listeners of all ages. His compositions are often characterized by a rich orchestration, catchy hooks, and foot-tapping beats, making them instant chartbusters.

 

The music maestro has collaborated with several top directors and actors in the South Indian film industry, including Gautham Menon, Shankar, and Suriya, among others. Some of his most popular tracks include "Engeyum Kadhal," "Vaaranam Aayiram," "Ghajini," and "Kaakha Kaakha," to name a few. Harris Jayaraj's music has not only entertained the masses but also earned him numerous awards and accolades, including several Filmfare Awards and Tamil Nadu State Film Awards.

 

Apart from Tamil films, Harris Jayaraj has also composed music for Telugu and Hindi movies, further expanding his reach and popularity. His versatility and ability to cater to different genres have made him a sought-after music composer in the industry.

item.title: M.M. Keeravani
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
M.M. Keeravani

Music Composer

M.M. Keeravani, also known as M.M. Kreem, is an Indian music composer and playback singer, primarily working in the Telugu and Hindi film industries. He has made a significant impact on the Indian music scene with his soulful compositions, making him one of the most respected and sought-after music composers in the industry.

 

Keeravani has an incredible ability to captivate the audience with his diverse range of music styles. He is known for his versatility, effortlessly shifting between various genres such as classical, folk, devotional, and western fusion. His compositions have a unique blend of traditional Indian elements and modern influences, creating a perfect harmony that appeals to a wide range of listeners.

 

Keeravani has composed music for numerous blockbuster films, such as the Baahubali series, Magadheera, and Rajanna, to name a few. The music of these films became immensely popular, with fans across the globe praising Keeravani for his exceptional talent. His ability to create melodies that are emotionally engaging and resonate with the storyline is truly remarkable.

 

Apart from his exceptional music compositions, Keeravani is also known for his soulful singing. He has lent his voice to several hit songs, adding an extra layer of emotion and depth to his compositions. His rich and powerful vocals have earned him a dedicated fan base, who eagerly await his every release.

 

M.M. Keeravani's contribution to the Indian music industry is unparalleled. His talent, passion, and dedication have made him a celebrated composer and singer. With his ability to create magical music that connects with the audience on a deep level, Keeravani continues to inspire and entertain millions of fans worldwide.

item.title: Meet Bros
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Meet Bros

Music Composer

Meet Bros is a renowned music composer duo in the Indian music industry. Comprising of brothers Manmeet and Harmeet Singh, they have made a significant mark with their melodious compositions and foot-tapping beats. With their unique style and creativity, Meet Bros have created a niche for themselves in the Bollywood music scene.

 

Known for their ability to blend various genres seamlessly, Meet Bros have produced a wide range of chart-topping songs that have become instant hits. They have composed music for numerous movies, making them one of the most sought-after composers in the industry. Their compositions have a distinct flavor, often incorporating elements of pop, rock, and electronic music, which sets them apart from their contemporaries.

 

Their collaboration with various talented singers has further added to their success. Meet Bros have worked with celebrated artists such as Arijit Singh, Neha Kakkar, Kanika Kapoor, and Mika Singh, among others, creating magic with their compositions. Their songs are known for their catchy tunes, meaningful lyrics, and the ability to resonate with the masses.

 

Apart from composing music for films, Meet Bros have also released their own independent singles, showcasing their versatility as artists. These tracks have received immense love and appreciation from fans across the globe. With their infectious energy and captivating stage presence, the duo has also become a favorite amongst audiences during live performances.

 

Meet Bros' contribution to the music industry has been recognized and awarded several times. They have won prestigious awards like the Filmfare Awards and the Zee Cine Awards for their exceptional compositions. Their success story is a testament to their hard work, talent, and commitment to creating soulful music.

item.title: Meghna Mishra
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Meghna Mishra

Music Composer

Meghna Mishra is an Indian playback singer known for her association with music director Amit Trivedi. She gained widespread recognition with her performances in the 2017 film Secret Superstar, where she delivered two superhit tracks, "Nachdi Phira" and "Main Kaun Hoon". The film starred Zaira Wasim, Meher Vij, and Aamir Khan.

 

Her song "Nachdi Phira" earned her the prestigious Best Female Playback Singer award at the 63rd Filmfare Awards. The track received immense acclaim for Meghna's soulful rendition and was hailed as one of the standout songs of the film. It showcased her versatility and ability to evoke emotions through her powerful vocals.

 

Another popular song from the film, "Main Kaun Hoon," was widely appreciated and resonated with the audience. It was included in the list of best Hindi songs of 2017 by an online portal. Composed by Amit Trivedi and with lyrics penned by Kausar Munir, the song showcased Meghna's ability to capture the essence of the character and deliver a heartfelt performance.

 

Meghna Mishra's association with Amit Trivedi has proven to be a successful collaboration, with her soul-stirring voice bringing life to his compositions. Her performances in Secret Superstar showcased her talent and garnered her critical acclaim. She captivated listeners with her ability to express a range of emotions through her vocals, leaving a lasting impact on the audience.

item.title: Mithun Sharma
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Mithun Sharma

Music Composer

Mithun Sharma, popularly known as Mithoon, is a talented music composer in the Indian music industry. Born on January 11, 1985, in Mumbai, India, Mithoon has achieved tremendous success and recognition for his soulful compositions that touch the hearts of millions.

 

Mithoon hails from a musical family as his father, Naresh Sharma, is a well-known music director. Growing up surrounded by music, Mithoon developed a deep passion for composing and started his journey at a young age. He gained formal training in music and honed his skills, eventually emerging as a prominent composer.

 

Mithoon's compositions are characterized by their emotional depth and soul-stirring melodies. His music often strikes a chord with listeners, evoking a range of emotions, from joy to sorrow. His ability to blend traditional Indian instruments with contemporary sounds and arrangements is commendable. Mithoon's work is a beautiful fusion of classical and modern music that appeals to a wide audience.

 

One of Mithoon's breakthrough compositions was the soulful track "Tum Hi Ho" from the movie "Aashiqui 2" (2013). This song became an instant sensation and catapulted Mithoon to great heights of fame. The haunting melody and heartfelt lyrics resonated with listeners, making it one of the most beloved romantic tracks of recent times.

 

Mithoon has collaborated with several renowned artists and filmmakers in the industry, delivering hit after hit. His notable works include compositions for movies like "Hamari Adhuri Kahani," "Half Girlfriend," and "Kabir Singh." Mithoon's music has garnered him numerous awards and accolades, including Filmfare and IIFA awards for Best Music Director.

item.title: Ouseppachan
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Ouseppachan

Music Composer

Ouseppachan, also known as K. J. Yesudas Ouseppachan, is a renowned Indian music composer who has left an indelible mark on the Malayalam film industry. Born on March 13, 1949, in Kozhikode, Kerala, he has been actively involved in the music industry for over four decades.

 

Ouseppachan's musical journey began at a young age when he started learning classical music. He later studied music at the Swathi Thirunal College of Music in Thiruvananthapuram. He made his debut as a music director in the Malayalam film industry with the movie "January Oru Orma" in 1987, and since then, there has been no turning back.

 

Ouseppachan is known for his versatility and ability to compose music that resonates with the audience. His compositions are a beautiful blend of classical and contemporary elements, which have garnered him immense appreciation and accolades throughout his career. He has worked on numerous hit films and has collaborated with some of the industry's finest filmmakers and lyricists.

 

What sets Ouseppachan apart is his ability to understand the nuances of storytelling and translate them into soul-stirring melodies. His music has the power to evoke emotions and create a lasting impact on the viewers. From foot-tapping numbers to heartwrenching ballads, he has showcased his talent across various genres and captivated the hearts of millions.

 

Ouseppachan's contributions to the Malayalam film industry have been recognized and honored with several awards, including the Kerala State Film Award for Best Music Director. His melodies have become timeless classics, and his music continues to be cherished by music lovers even today.
